headline: Lateef Bhat’s killing marks end of India-born terrorist presence in Kashmir: Amit Shah
content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday said that Kashmir had become free of India-born terrorists following the killing of Lashkar-e-Toiba (LeT) commander Mohammed Lateef Bhat in Kulgam, describing it as a significant development after 35 years of militancy in the Valley.Addressing the inaugural session of a two-day counter-terrorism conference organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), Shah said the government was putting in place a uniform strategy to combat terrorism, extending down to the level of every police station across the country.Referring to recent successful operations, Shah said these had strengthened the country's confidence in its fight against terrorism.He said the hallmark of an effective security agency was to identify and apprehend terrorists before they could execute an attack. Police forces across states should study and implement this model, he added.The Home Minister also pointed out that the Pakistan-based Shahzad Bhatti network has been declared a terrorist organisation under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) and more than 40 of its modules have been neutralised across the country. In the action taken against this network, over 100 cases have been registered and more than 271 arrests have been made, he informed further.Shah said India had been confronting terrorism for decades, but a lack of coordination among state police forces and central agencies had earlier hampered efforts. The government was now working towards a coordinated national framework with clearly defined responsibilities at every level.Emphasising the need to dismantle the entire terror ecosystem, Shah said more than 303 fugitives had been brought back to India from 36 countries since 2019. He also stressed the importance of targeting terror financing networks through better coordination with financial investigation agencies.He called for a proactive approach to counter-terrorism, directing states to strengthen their Anti-Terrorism Squads (ATS) and cyber expertise. Investigations, he said, must continue until the entire network behind a terror incident was dismantled.Shah also highlighted the expansion of the NIA, saying approval had been granted for 16 new branch offices and two zonal offices. The agency's legal powers had also been enhanced, including its mandate to investigate cases concerning the interests of Indians living abroad.Referring to the action against the Popular Front of India (PFI), he said coordinated operations involving police forces from 11 states and central agencies had significantly weakened its network.On the occasion, Shah released the NIA publication ‘Fail-Safe Investigation’ and laid the foundation stone for the agency's office complex in Chandigarh.

headline: Yogi urges Gen Z to revisit pre-2017 govt terms as BJP sharpens youth outreach
content: UP CM Yogi Adityanath’s remarks on Wednesday echoed the BJP’s wider plan to shape youth perceptions of previous non-BJP governments, placing law and order, identity and development at the centre of its political narrative.Yogi’s appeal to Gen Z and Gen Alpha to understand what the state was like a decade ago was more than an attempt to recall its law-and-order problems. It reflects a broader political effort by the BJP to make the experience of previous governments part of the political consciousness of a generation that has little or no direct memory of that period.The CM said young people, particularly those aged between 15 and 27, needed to know about the alleged atmosphere of riots, prolonged curfews, criminal intimidation and insecurity for women and traders before the BJP came to power in 2017.His remarks assume significance against the backdrop of what The Tribune had first reported about the BJP’s plan to familiarise young people with the ill-record of non-BJP governments. The broader political objective is to make governance under previous dispensations a subject of discussion among first-time and younger voters, rather than allowing their political understanding to be shaped only by their own experiences of the present government.To reinforce the contrast, he cited the Muzaffarnagar riots, the Jawahar Bagh violence and incidents in Kosi Kalan, Aligarh and Bareilly during the Samajwadi Party’s tenure. He also invoked the killing of police officers during the Jawahar Bagh operation.

headline: Shiv Sena’s focus is on improving its base in Pune ahead of 2029 elections, not to challenge other partie
content: Pune: State industries minister and Shiv Sena senior Uday Samant on Thursday said the party would work towards strengthening its base in the district with a view to the 2029 elections.Samant’s comment came against the backdrop of Shiv Sena’s decision to support a rebel candidate against BJP’s official nominee for the Pune teachers’ constituency in the recently concluded state MLC polls. Clarifying his party’s stand, Samant said, “Shiv Sena is not challenging any party, but is looking to grow its base in Pune.”Along with Legislative Council deputy chairperson Sachin Ahir, Samant held a series of meetings with party functionaries in Baramati, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) and Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (PCMC) limits on Thursday.The outreach assumes significance as Shiv Sena failed to win a single seat in last year’s PMC elections. Following the poor showing, the party reorganised its local unit and entrusted Samant with the task of rebuilding its organisation in the region.Addressing party workers after the meetings, Samant indicated further restructuring of local units in the coming months. “The Shiv Sena chief has given me the responsibility to grow the party in Baramati, Pune and Pimpri Chinchwad. While we are looking to expand our party’s base, we will continue to work unitedly in Mahayuti,” Samant said.The meetings form part of the party’s broader strategy to expand its footprint in western Maharashtra while maintaining its alliance with Mahayuti partners.

headline: Former-Tamil Nadu minister, government officials named in ₹1,427-crore sand mining case | Hindustan Times
content: Former Tamil Nadu minister Durai Murugan and several government officials have been named as accused in an illegal sand mining case that caused a ₹1,427-crore loss to the state exchequer, officials aware of the development in the Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) said.Murugan, 88, is the general secretary of the DMK, the principal Opposition party in the state assembly. In the April 23 Assembly polls, he lost to TVK candidate M Sudhakar in his home constituency of Katpadi.Also read: Ex-AIADMK minister C Vijayabaskar quizzed by ED in disproportionate assets case ED report flags alleged illegal mining at 28 quarry sitesAccording to the First Information Report (FIR) accessed by HT, the joint director, Chennai zone, Directorate of Enforcement, sent a report on June 13, 2024, to the director general of police of Tamil Nadu, alleging that illegal river sand mining had taken place at 28 quarry sites in the state between 2021 and 2024.The mining was conducted in collusion with senior officials of the Water Resources Department, the mining department and local bodies, at the instance of Murugan, who was then minister for the Water Resources Department, the FIR stated. A detailed inquiry registered on December 12, 2025 named three private individuals and contractors who were allegedly also involved in the illegal sand mining at all 28 sites.

headline: Shinde Sena meet to condemn Sonia’s “insult” of Savarkar ends with Shaina NC tearing Bal Thackeray photo | Mumbai news
content: MUMBAI: A meeting called on Wednesday by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena to protest against Sonia Gandhi’s “insult” of Hindutva idealogue V D Savarkar in her autobiography saw a bizarre and comedic twist when Sena spokesperson Shaina N C allegedly tore a picture of Bal Thackeray and found herself at the receiving end of protests by the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena (UBT). While Shaina denied tearing Thackeray’s picture, the incident set off a swirl of retaliation and counter-retaliation on social media and the streets.The cascading chain of events began after Sena national spokesperson Sanjay Nirupam read from Sonia’s recently released autobiography ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’. An excerpt that had the party in a flap was: ‘While Congress freedom fighters were enduring assaults and imprisonment at the hands of the British rulers, senior ideologues of the RSS like Vinayak Damodar Savarkar were writing mercy petitions to their colonial masters, and their members were colluding with the British authorities as informers.’“The book shows Sonia’s hatred towards revolutionary freedom fighter Savarkar,” said Nirupam. “Indira Gandhi contributed towards a Savarkar memorial, but Sonia exhibited a hatred for Savarkar to get Muslim votes. She opposed a portrait of Savarkar in Parliament and wrote a letter to the then president APJ Abdul Kalam to not allow this. I demand a ban on her book.”The party’s six spokespersons then protested by tearing pages from the memoir. In the melee, Shaina reportedly tore a separate photograph which the Shinde Sena had brought along to show how Sena founder Bal Thackeray had slapped an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar for his comments on Savarkar. Shaina, however, maintained that she “only tore Mani Shankar Aiyar’s picture, and this is what the late Balasaheb would have done”. As the Sena (UBT) protest against her intensified, she posted on X: ‘Show me where I have torn or disrespected Hinduhrudaysamrat Balasaheb Thackeray’s photograph. Deliberately twisting an incident to create a false narrative will not be tolerated. Anyone spreading defamatory claims against me will face legal action. And yes, as I have said, I will tear Manishankar Aiyar’s photograph a thousand times over and this is what Balasaheb taught us.’Shinde also denied that Thackeray’s photo was torn up. “Shaina has shown me what she tore,” he said. “No one from my party would ever insult Balasaheb.Apart from Shaina, Sena spokespersons Anand Dube, Susiben Shah, Sheetal Mhatre and Sanjana Ghadi also addressed the press conference. While Shaina demanded that the publishers delete pages 201 and 443 which “insult” Savarkar, Mhatre sought to know the reaction of Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray. “I wish to know whether this insult is acceptable to him,” she said. “Will he slap an effigy of Sonia Gandhi? I am waiting for the Sena (UBT) stand on this issue.”.Responding to the Sena spokespersons’ allegations, Congress spokesperson Atul Londhe said, “Savarkar’s grandson himself has accepted that Savarkar wrote a mercy petition. Soniaji has presented facts. The RSS, which admired Adolf Hitler, has always aimed to create a Hindu nation, with people of other faiths being relegated to second-class citizenship. And it has always seen the Congress as a stumbling block in the path of this aim.”Slamming Shinde’s colleagues for tearing Bal Thackeray’s picture, Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut posted on social media: ‘Amit Shah’s Shinde Sena supporters are tearing up a photo of Shiv Sena chief Balasaheb Thackeray… These people have no ideology or morals, no single leader or loyalty… All these people who insulted Balasaheb should be publicly flogged.”The incident echoed in the civic body where Sena (UBT) corporators protested at the BMC meeting. Raising slogans against the Shinde Sena in the corridor, a group of workers even went to their Nariman Point headquarters Balasaheb Bhavan to raise slogans there. “These people run the party on Balasaheb’s name and then tear his picture,” said Kishori Pednekar, leader of the opposition in the BMC.While BJP leader Pravin Darekar said, “Those agitating must be more cautious. They should apologise if they have torn Bal Thackeray’s photo accidentally.”

headline: ‘Symbol of indomitable courage, strong leadership’: Congress salutes Indira Gandhi on birth anniversary
content: <p>New Delhi: Indira Gandhi was a revolutionary and continued to be one in government, making big decisions with fervour, love and commitment to her country, says Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra in a video shared by her mother <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/sonia-gandhi">Sonia Gandhi </a>on former prime minister's birth anniversary on Thursday.</p><p><a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/congress">Congress </a>Parliamentary Chairperson Sonia Gandhi also recalled her first meeting with Indira Gandhi.</p><p>In a post on X, Sonia Gandhi said, "The first time I was to meet Indira Gandhi, I refused to go. The next day I changed my mind. I was terribly nervous, and my English was poor, so she spoke to me in French. That was the first thing I learnt about her: she noticed what you were struggling with and quietly made it easier.</p><p>"The world knew the Prime Minister. At home we knew Dadi -- a loving and gentle person, full of stories and wisdom and an incredible sense of humour," she said of her mother-in-law.</p><p>"Some of her lives on in all of us, whether we know it or not. We still miss her," Sonia Gandhi said.</p>.'Happy Birthday, tigress': Priyanka hails Indira Gandhi on 109th birth anniversary.<p>She also shared a video of a conversation she had a few days ago with daughter Priyanka and granddaughter Miraya Vadra at 1, Safdarjung Road house, where Indira Gandhi lived as PM.</p><p>In the video titled 'The Indira the world never saw', the three of them are seen sitting in the garden of 1, Safdarjung Road, and recalling what Indira Gandhi was like at home.</p><p>"I was married in that corner. The table was there where we signed the papers. That's where we were married," says Sonia Gandhi, pointing to the part of the house where her marriage took place.</p><p>"It was a very small wedding. My mother-in-law got all the clans involved - the Nehru clan, the Katju clan, the Kaul clan," she recalls.</p><p>Talking about her wedding and adjusting in a new home, Sonia Gandhi says it was like most Indian women when they get married and go into a new home and have to adjust.</p><p>"It was not all easy, because everyone was looking at me to see if I was doing it right. I had a feeling that I was being watched, not within the family, but outside," she says in the video shot before Diwali.</p><p>Talking about her first meeting with Indira Gandhi, Sonia Gandhi says, "Within the family, she was never tough with you. She would not say 'do this' or 'do that', she was sort of working around it. She was very disciplined - she was a working woman, so she would start at the crack of dawn. I was kind of in awe of her. I didn't know how to approach, what to say, what not to say in the beginning.</p>.Until I got to know her well, I'd quake in my seat: Sonia Gandhi on Indira Gandhi's temper.<p>"I met her in London when Nana (Rajiv Gandhi) had written to her that he had met this girl whom he liked, loved, and wanted to marry. She was passing through London for two days and wrote to say she wanted to meet me.</p><p>"From Cambridge halfway to London, I had a panic fit. I said, 'No, I am not going to meet your mother.' We looked for a red telephone booth, called where she was staying at the High Commission, and found an excuse.</p><p>"A day later, I prepared myself and we went up to where she was staying. She was lying down, very tired and jetlagged. She started asking me about myself. I spoke in French because my English was non-existent," Sonia Gandhi recounts.</p><p>Sonia Gandhi says it took quite some time for her to become close because everything was a cultural shock.</p><p>"What was helpful was that she had been abroad as a student - as a little girl when her mother was sick in Switzerland, then at school in England and Oxford. So she understood Western ways," Sonia Gandhi says.</p><p>"Because she was a working woman engaged 24/7 in her work, the daughter-in-law could be a little more relaxed. Later, she was inspiring - I learned a lot from her. She was courageous and determined to follow her ideological principles above all. She was relaxed as a mother-in-law; there weren't things like 'you must do this, you can't do that'," she says.</p><p>Reminiscing about her grandmother, Priyanka says Indira Gandhi was very loving as a grandmother.</p><p>"There were many non-negotiable rules in our house that we had to live within. She was the primary enforcer; secondary was my father, my mother was lenient. We were scared if she got angry, but she was also very gentle and loving," Priyanka says of Indira Gandhi.</p><p>"She would make us play games all the time - like the capital game. She had breakfast with us before school, came back from parliament or work for lunch and dinner, and spent Sundays with us. She told stories about Joan of Arc, the independence movement, her childhood, and talked politics with Rahul," Priyanka recalls.</p><p>Indira Gandhi played little tricks and pranks on us, like hiding behind something and jumping out, she further recounts.</p><p>Sonia recalls that on birthdays, Indira Gandhi would bring out Bengali mud toys that looked like real insects and put them on the table as a prank.</p><p>Hailing Indira Gandhi, Priyanka says, "As a child, I just wanted to be her. Everybody was scared of her, but she was brave and bright. Today as a woman, I think about her journey from when her entire family was in prison fighting for freedom.</p><p>"She was a revolutionary and continued to be one even in government, making big decisions with that same fervor, love, and commitment to her country," she says.</p><p>Indira Gandhi was born on November 19, 1917, in Prayagraj. She was assassinated on October 31, 1984, in New Delhi.</p><p>She served as the prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984.</p>

headline: PM Modi uses GTA 6 vs GTA 5 comparison to pitch India's growth; Congress mocks move
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday invoked the popular video game Grand Theft Auto (GTA) to showcase India's development over the past 12 years, drawing a sarcastic response from the Congress, which pointed to the game's "criminal duo".Taking to social media, Modi wrote, “India is playing a whole new game,” and shared 10 slides titled “Between GTA V and VI, here's how”.In an apparent attempt to connect with younger audiences, Modi used the slides to draw a comparison in development work witnessed by India between the two instalments of the game..An action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI was rolled out across the globe on Thursday, marking its entry into the GTA series following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V.Modi drew parallels between GTA 5, launched in 2013-14 when the previous UPA government was in power, and GTA 6, released on Thursday under the Modi-led NDA dispensation, to highlight changes in various development parameters."Between GTA 5 and 6, here is how India upgraded," he said in a social media post featuring illustrations of an aeroplane, train, rocket, solar station, mobile phone, road network and ship, among others.The prime minister said India, once described as part of the "fragile five" economies, was now the world's fastest-growing economy. He also said poverty had declined from 27 per cent, with extreme poverty now reduced to 2.6 per cent.Referring to the Swachh Bharat campaign and the construction of toilets, particularly for women, Modi said sanitation coverage had risen from 39 per cent to 100 per cent. On the energy front, he said India's solar capacity had increased from 2.82 GW to 175 GW.Highlighting the growth of the space sector, Modi said India now had 440 space startups, compared with none in the earlier period. Railway electrification, he said, had increased from 20 per cent to 99.6 per cent, while the cost of 1 GB of 3G internet had fallen from Rs 308 to Rs 7.51.The prime minister also said India, once a major importer of defence equipment, now exported arms and defence equipment to more than 80 countries. On the security front, Modi said the number of Naxal-affected districts had also declined. "Then, 182 districts (were) Naxal affected, now zero district," he said.The Congress took a swipe at Modi over his use of GTA imagery, with party general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh saying it was appropriate given the game's storyline.Ramesh said, “The PM, in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth, has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media.”“Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate,” he said on X.(With inputs from PTI).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: AAP puts Bhagwant Mann at centre of Punjab billboard campaign ahead of 2027 polls
content: CHANDIGARH: Billboards featuring Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann with slogans such as "Imaandar CM" (Honest Chief Minister), "Lokan Da CM" (Chief Minister of the masses) and "AAP Da Ikko Naara Bhagwant Mann Dobara" (AAP's only slogan is Bhagwant Mann again) have appeared across Punjab, in what appears to be an attempt by the ruling party to project Mann as the face of the government and counter the Opposition's narrative that the state is being run from Delhi.With Mann sporting his trademark yellow turban, the hoardings have turned roads and public spaces across the state into a political messaging platform ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The campaign seeks to highlight his personal image, public outreach and the government's welfare initiatives.The publicity drive comes as the AAP positions Mann as its principal face for the next Assembly elections. For much of the past four-and-a-half years, AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal and state in-charge Manish Sisodia were frequently seen in Punjab, attending the launches of key government initiatives, including the Yudh Nashian Virudh (anti-drug campaign) and Aam Aadmi Clinics.In January this year, Kejriwal and Mann jointly launched the Mukh Mantri Sehat Yojana, which provides free cashless treatment of up to Rs 10 lakh to every family. In April last year, Sisodia led the 54-day Sikhiya Kranti education drive to upgrade around 12,000 government schools, reinforcing the perception that key political initiatives were being led from Delhi.However, Kejriwal and Sisodia were noticeably absent during the recently concluded Asian Hockey Champions Trophy matches in Jalandhar and Mohali and the Diwali celebrations.During the run-up to the 2022 Assembly elections, Kejriwal had shared billboards with Mann and, at times, overshadowed him. This time, his photograph appears only on posters put up by ticket aspirants..Punjab CM Mann launches AAP door-to-door campaign with governance report card ahead of 2027 polls.The billboard campaign has also triggered a counter-campaign by the Opposition. While the AAP government is promoting Mann through the "Imaandar CM" slogan, hoardings challenging his claims on development and road construction have appeared in different parts of the state. One billboard in Barnala claims that a road was built by the Chief Minister, while another in Ropar takes the opposite position, stating that the road was not constructed by Mann.Meanwhile, Mann has been holding Lok Milni (public meetings), repeatedly claiming that his government has fulfilled all its promises and gone beyond them. He has also been highlighting initiatives such as the provision of 600 units of free electricity to eligible households.The campaign comes amid controversies involving the Chief Minister's office and family. In October, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) booked Mann's Officer on Special Duty (OSD), Rajbir Singh Ghuman, in an alleged corruption case involving manipulation of officers' transfers and postings, tenders and policy decisions, as well as the leaking of confidential files. Ghuman has undergone multiple rounds of questioning.Ghuman has denied any wrongdoing, saying he is cooperating with the investigation. He has also alleged political pressure aimed at targeting the Chief Minister and his office. Mann and the AAP have similarly accused central agencies of being misused for political purposes.In August this year, allegations surfaced that Mann's wife, Dr Gurpreet Kaur Mann, had sought a Rs 5-crore bribe to suppress or settle a rape case. Both she and the AAP have strongly denied the allegations, which remain unproven. Kaur has filed a defamation case against Akali Dal leader Bikram Majithia and Congress MLA Sukhpal Khaira, with court proceedings underway.The billboard campaign has drawn criticism from the Congress, BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), with Opposition leaders questioning the need for repeated declarations of honesty and the public expenditure involved..AAP to launch door-to-door campaign in Punjab; Manish Sisodia says will return with bigger mandate .Defending the campaign, AAP spokesperson Baltej Singh Pannu said the Opposition had no substantive issues to raise and was making an issue out of billboards, which, he said, were used by all political parties."They cannot give answers to 300 units of free power, water reaching farmers at tale ends, Mohala clinics and the welfare scheme implemented by our government," he said.Punjab BJP spokesperson Pritpal Singh Baliwal questioned the need for the campaign, saying, "if a Chief Minister has to put billboards to tell the public that his honest that means his government is not? Already two his cabinet colleagues are behind bars and there are allegations on the his kin and he claims he is honest."Congress MLA Sukhpal Singh Khaira also criticised the campaign, saying, "For first time in 70-years In never have seen in my political carrier that a Chief Minister has to put billboards to tell that he is honest, as honesty is in one’s character and is displayed in one’s working and not written on boards."SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal also criticised Mann over the roadside billboards portraying him as an honest Chief Minister, alleging that crores of rupees of public money had been spent on the publicity campaign..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Congress Dares Shiv Sena to Tear Golwalkar’s Book ‘Bunch of Thoughts’
content: Congress National Secretary Sachin Sawant on Thursday countered protests by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena against a book on Sonia Gandhi by citing writings from former RSS chief MS Golwalkar regarding Hindutva ideologue V.D. Savarkar. He challenged the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena to tear up Golwalkar’s book ‘Bunch of Thoughts,’ claiming it contains criticisms of Savarkar. Questioning the Shinde Shiv Sena’s outrage over Sonia Gandhi’s book, Sawant said the second RSS Chief MS Golwalkar had criticised Savarkar’s brand of Hindutva as negative and described him as a ‘traitor’ (rashtradrohi) in his book ‘Bunch of Thoughts.’ He asked whether the Shiv Sena would tear Golwalkar’s book and exit the ruling Mahayuti coalition aligned with the RSS’ ideology. Sawant also cited former BJP leader and ex-Union Minister Arun Shourie’s book ‘The New Icon: Savarkar and the Facts,’ saying it also examines historical records and claims regarding Savarkar. The Congress leader added that Sonia Gandhi’s reference to Savarkar on page 201 of ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’ reflects historical reality and aligns with her lifelong political commitment to Mahatma Gandhi’s principles of truth and non-violence. He claimed that in the defamation case filed by Savarkar’s relative Satyaki Savarkar against Rahul Gandhi in a Pune court, Satyaki had acknowledged that Savarkar submitted ten mercy petitions (mafinamas). Sawant’s statement comes after Sonia Gandhi’s autobiography, ‘Belonging: A Journey of Love’, triggered political pushback in Maharashtra over references on Savarkar’s mercy petitions to British authorities and the historical role of the RSS. The Eknath Shinde’s Shiv Sena staged demonstrations in Mumbai, tore pages from the book, demanded a ban on it and sought an apology from Shiv Sena-UBT Chief Uddhav Thackeray. Meanwhile, Ranjit Savarkar, social activist, and the grandnephew of VD Savarkar has alleged that Sonia Gandhi in her book has made derogatory remarks about VD Savarkar. Accusing former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru of imposing partition on the country, he said, “If Sonia Gandhi continues to propagate false information regarding Swatantryaveer Savarkar, then Nehru’s own dark deeds will be brought to light.” Ranjit Savarkar said, “Sonia Gandhi fails to mention how Nehru agreed to the proposal for the partition of the country. The very plan that was rejected on May 10, 1947, was accepted by Nehru following his interactions with Lord Mountbatten. What led Nehru to accept a plan he had previously rejected? Sonia Gandhi ought to have researched what transpired during the two days of May 11 and May 12, 1947.” “Swayed by his infatuation with Lady Mountbatten, Nehru imposed the partition upon the nation. More than two million Hindus were killed in the ensuing riots. In her book, Pamela Mountbatten – daughter of Lord Mountbatten – mentions that while serving as Prime Minister, Nehru regularly sent letters to Lady Mountbatten, detailing his daily activities and expressing his romantic affections. These letters were once available at the Nehru Museum in Delhi; however, they disappeared after Sonia Gandhi became the President of the Congress party,” Ranjit Savarkar said.

headline: Odisha Assembly Adjourned Till 4 PM Over Ganjam Flood, Kotia Row
content: Bhubaneswar: The Odisha Assembly was adjourned till 4 pm on Thursday as opposition BJD and Congress members created a ruckus demanding a detailed discussion on the recent flood in Ganjam district and the Kotia border dispute with neighbouring Andhra Pradesh.The pandemonium started as soon as the House assembled for Question Hour at 10.30 am. The agitating opposition MLAs were already in the well of the House before Speaker Surama Padhy took her seat.As Padhy allowed Parliamentary Affairs Minister Mukesh Mahaling to reply to a question, the opposition members raised slogans, creating a noisy scene. While some members were seen standing on the reporters' table, a section of agitating lawmakers was shouting below the Speaker's podium.Congress member Taraprasad Bahinipati was seen banging the Speaker's podium while shouting slogans against the BJP government in the state.Members of both the BJD and the Congress displayed placards in the House and demanded discussion on their respective demands. While the BJD demanded a debate on the Ganjam flood, the Congress MLAs raised the Kotia border dispute with Andhra Pradesh.The House could transact business for only seven minutes amid din before the Speaker adjourned the House till 4 pm.BJD MLA Sarada Prasanna Jena said, "The BJD has submitted a motion to the Speaker a day before the commencement of the session for a discussion on the flood issue after suspending all the business of the House. However, the Speaker did not pay heed to our notice. Therefore, there is no alternative but to demand a discussion."

headline: Harish In Touch With BJP Before Polls: CM
content: Hyderabad:Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy on Thursday launched a scathing attack on senior BRS leader and Siddipet MLA T. Harish Rao, alleging that he was in touch with the BJP and would leave the BRS before the 2028 Assembly elections.Addressing a public meeting in Siddipet after launching the Indiramma Family Life Insurance Scheme, offering free life insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh to more than one crore families across Telangana, Revanth Reddy challenged Harish Rao to take an oath in the name of Siddipet Yellamma that he would not join the BJP, if the allegation was false.Revanth Reddy also indirectly targeted two Congress MLAs, who have recently criticised the Congress government, referring to them as "persons bitten by mad dogs" and saying Congress activists would soon take them to Erragadda hospital for treatment, without naming Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy and Jadcherla MLA J. Anirudh Reddy.The Chief Minister alleged that Harish Rao was planning to backstab BRS president K. Chandrashekar Rao by quitting the party and joining the BJP. He said Chandrashekhar Rao's fate was only a reflection of his own political history, alleging that he had betrayed the Congress and the Telugu Desam after they had given him political opportunities, including Assembly tickets, and helped him become an MLA and minister.The Chief Minister said Siddipet Congress leader A. Madan Mohan Rao had played a key role in keeping the Congress flag flying in Siddipet until 1985 and accused Chandrashekhar Rao and Harish Rao of attempting to erase his name from history. He directed health minister Damodar Rajanarsimha to name Siddipet Medical College after Madan Mohan Rao.Revanth Reddy said Harish Rao was not even a ward member in 2004 but became a minister and Siddipet MLA with the political blessing of late Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy.He alleged that Chandrashekar Rao, K.T. Rama Rao and Harish Rao had looted Telangana during the BRS’ 10-year rule and appealed to Siddipet voters to elect the Congress candidate in the next Assembly election. He promised that the Congress candidate elected from Siddipet would be made a minister in the next Congress government in 2029.The Chief Minister recalled the political legacy of leaders from Medak district such as Madan Mohan Rao, Cheruku Muthyam Reddy and Solipeta Ramalinga Reddy and compared their political and financial circumstances with those of Chandrashekhar Rao, Rama Rao and Harish Rao. He questioned how the top 3 BRS leaders could have accumulated "thousands of crores" when their close associate like Ramalinga Reddy had died leaving his family in difficult financial circumstances.Revanth Reddy described Chandrashekar Rao, Harish Rao, Rama Rao and J. Santosh Rao as a quartet responsible for exploiting Telangana's resources and alleged that even commissions were taken in the distribution of Bathukamma sareesHe said the BRS had a past but no future and asserted that Indiramma Rajyam would continue until 2034. He also questioned whether Siddipet should remain under the control of one political family. Revanth Reddy said he was a son of Telangana who was born on its soil and would remain part of it, and questioned why he would ever do injustice to the State or the people who had blessed him.

headline: Kerala CM Walks a Tightrope Between Image and Governance
content: Thiruvananthapuram: Kerala's Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan is moving swiftly. In just six months, the 62-year-old leader has begun positioning himself as the Congress's next mass figure, aiming to fill the space once occupied by Oommen Chandy and A. K. Antony.Many view accessibility as his hallmark. Ordinary citizens can approach him without navigating layers of security or being turned away by commandos. Supporters see in him a leader who genuinely listens.However, critics, primarily from the CPM, argue that this is carefully crafted image-making rather than a natural style.Several early decisions have resonated with the common people. The Priyadarshini scheme provides free travel for women on KSRTC buses, an exclusive department for the elderly has been established, and honoraria for ASHA workers and mid-day meal staff have been increased. These measures demonstrate attention to the needs of the poor and overlooked.ASHA workers, who had protested for 265 days under the previous left government without results, finally received a response. The CPM has taken note of the public goodwill generated by these measures, focusing its counterattack on Satheesan's style—accusing him of arrogance and of making decisions without consulting UDF allies. The Marxists also allege that he is aligning with Modi's economic policies to undermine the "Kerala Model" of development. Tensions exist within the UDF and Congress as well. UDF convenor Adoor Prakash publicly expressed frustration that he often learns about major government decisions only through the media.Prakash even traveled to Delhi to register his protest, but the high command chose not to intervene. The government is still young and delivering on its promises, yet a strong internal lobby remains uneasy with Satheesan. It is widely known that this group has the quiet backing of A general secretary K. C. Venugopal, who was the Congress legislators' first choice for the top post. Satheesan secured the position largely due to public support and his successful tenure as Opposition Leader. Many MLAs now back him because they have little alternative. Venugopal, who represents Alappuzha constituency in the Lok Sabha, continues to make regular visits to Kerala, staying in touch with party workers and closely monitoring the government.Beyond Congress, the BJP is advancing its own strategy. Following impressive wins in three seats in the last assembly elections, including two in OBC-majority areas, the party is working to extend its reach beyond its traditional upper-caste Nair base into Ezhava and Dalit communities.Success here could significantly erode the CPM's core support. Currently, the BJP appears more focused on challenging the CPM than Congress, targeting Left strongholds politically, culturally, and within communities. The CPM is aware of the RSS-BJP efforts on the ground and is mounting its own countermeasures.One recent development has bolstered Satheesan's standing. The Nair Service Society (NSS), previously critical of him, has now publicly reconciled. NSS general secretary R. Sukumaran Nair, formerly a strong opponent, has invited Satheesan to visit the NSS headquarters in Perunna on January 2, 2027, to inaugurate the 150th birth anniversary celebrations of Mannathu Padmanabhan.Political observers believe Satheesan is relatively secure until the 2029 Lok Sabha elections. He understands the stakes: Congress must at least retain its 2024 seats and, ideally, make gains. A poor performance, particularly with Rahul Gandhi positioned as the main national challenger to Narendra Modi, could leave Satheesan in a situation similar to A. K. Antony in the 2004 Lok Sabha polls, when Congress suffered a rout in Kerala and the Chief Minister subsequently resigned. For now, Satheesan is relying on visible governance and direct engagement with the public to counter both external criticism and internal dissent.

headline: ₹71,000 Reward For Slapping Shaina NC: Shiv Sena (UBT) Leader Makes Announcement In Pimpri-Chinchwad; Says
content: Pimpri-Chinchwad: Shiv Sena (UBT) Pimpri-Chinchwad city president Chetan Pawar on Thursday announced a cash reward of ₹71,000 for anyone who slaps Shaina NC, national spokesperson and national secretary of the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.The announcement comes amid an escalating political row over the alleged tearing of a photograph of Shiv Sena founder Balasaheb Thackeray by Shaina during a protest in Mumbai.Watch Video:Speaking to the media on Thursday, Pawar said a reward of ₹1 lakh had already been announced by a Shiv Sena (UBT) functionary in Mumbai. He said the Pimpri-Chinchwad unit would offer an additional ₹71,000 in cash to anyone who slaps Shaina.“We are announcing that whoever slaps Shaina NC will be given ₹71,000 in cash on behalf of the Pimpri-Chinchwad city Shiv Sena (UBT),” Pawar said.However, Pawar also claimed that his party had always upheld the dignity and honour of women. He said assaulting a woman was not right and that the party would continue to respect women.In the same statement, he questioned Shaina's understanding of Balasaheb Thackeray's ideology. He said there was nothing to learn from someone who had no awareness of these issues.Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photographThe controversy began on Wednesday during a press conference organised by the Shinde-led Shiv Sena in Mumbai to protest against references to Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.During the protest, party leaders tore pages from the book. Shaina was also seen tearing a photograph showing Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper. The incident was caught on camera and triggered criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Pune: FDA Orders 8 JM Road Eateries To Shut, Suspends Licences Of 6 Others Over Hygiene ViolationsShaina, however, denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb. She maintained that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not Balasaheb's photograph. Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister and Shiv Sena leader Eknath Shinde also defended her explanation.On Thursday, Shaina apologised to Balasaheb's admirers if her actions had hurt their feelings, while maintaining that she had never intended to disrespect the late Shiv Sena founder.The incident has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde.

headline: Shaina NC Apologises Amid Bal Thackeray Photo Controversy, Shiv Sena (UBT) Workers Stage Protest Outside Sena
content: Mumbai: The controversy over Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC allegedly tearing a photograph of party founder Bal Thackeray escalated on Thursday, with hundreds of Shiv Sena (UBT) workers staging a protest outside Sena Bhavan in Dadar. The protesters demanded an FIR against her, while several demonstrators were detained by police. Amid the mounting backlash, Shaina issued an apology on social media, saying she never intended to disrespect the late leader.Shaina Expresses Regret Over IncidentIn a post on X, Shaina said her actions and statements had been deliberately misinterpreted. Describing Bal Thackeray as a towering nationalist leader whose ideology and commitment to Hindutva continued to inspire her, she said she understood the deep respect and affection people had for him.She expressed regret if her actions had unintentionally hurt the sentiments of genuine Shiv Sainiks and admirers of Bal Thackeray. However, she also hit back at her critics, saying she did not need anyone's certificate to prove her loyalty and affection towards the Sena founder and accused political opponents of exploiting the incident for political gains.Sena UBT Workers Demand Police ActionHundreds of Sena (UBT) supporters, including women, gathered outside the party headquarters and raised slogans against Shaina, demanding police action. Heavy police deployment was made to maintain law and order, and several protesters were detained, an official said.Mumbai: Sena UBT Leaders Hit Shaina NC's Poster With Slippers, Burn Photo Over Balasaheb Thackeray Row | VIDEOControversy Erupts During Press ConferenceThe controversy erupted on Wednesday during a press conference organised by the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena to protest against Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love'. The Shinde Sena leaders were objecting to Gandhi's remarks about Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar and the RSS.During the event, party leaders, including Shaina, tore copies of the book. However, Shaina allegedly tore a paper bearing a photograph of Bal Thackeray, who was seen slapping an effigy of former Union minister Mani Shankar Aiyar. A video of the incident went viral, triggering criticism from the Opposition.Also Watch:Political Parties Criticise IncidentShaina had initially maintained that she had torn Aiyar's photograph and not that of Bal Thackeray. headline: Tax cuts given, but where are jobs, higher wages? PM Modi asks India Inc
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday questioned whether India Inc had done enough to increase employment and employee incomes following corporate tax reductions and other government reforms, calling on businesses to assess how policy benefits had contributed to broader economic gains. Addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry's (Ficci's) annual general meeting at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, PM Modi urged companies to evaluate their contribution to employment generation, investment and India's long-term economic development. He highlighted the government's tax relief measures, stating there is no income tax on annual earnings up to ₹12 lakh. He added that purchasing power had increased and tax return filing and refunds had been made easier, ensuring that taxpayers' money was not held up. Under the current government, the baseline corporate tax rate for existing domestic companies was reduced from 30 per cent to 22 per cent (25.17 per cent effective rate, including surcharge and cess) in September 2019. A 15 per cent base rate was also introduced for eligible new domestic manufacturing companies. PM Modi invites suggestions from India Inc PM Modi also asked India Inc to suggest further reforms needed to accelerate the country's growth. He urged businesses to focus on making India self-reliant and invest more in agriculture and allied sectors. ALSO READ: Centre proposes separate wholesale licensing framework for bulk drugs "Without hesitation or reservation, please write to me openly about what still needs to be improved," the Prime Minister said, reported news agency PTI. He called on companies to adopt an 'India First' approach when making investment decisions over the next two decades, saying this would help make the country self-reliant while opening up new growth opportunities for businesses. PM Modi highlights poverty reduction PM Modi said India's pace of progress was very fast, while the rate at which people were moving out of poverty was also accelerating. Citing the latest World Bank report, he said that 50 crore people had overcome poverty in just 12-13 years. The Prime Minister also emphasised that a country progresses when it respects its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers, not by hurling abuses day in and day out.

headline: PM Modi invites suggestions from India Inc on reforms to drive growth
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday asked India Inc to suggest, without any hesitation or reluctance, more reforms that are necessary for further growth of the country.Addressing industry body FICCI' Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention, the prime minister also asked corporates to focus on making India self-reliant, and urged them to invest heavily in agriculture and allied sectors.Modi highlighted achievements of his government in the last 12-13 years, and lauded efforts made by all sections of the society.He said the pace of progress in India is very fast, and at the same time, the speed at which people are moving out of poverty is also very fast.Citing the latest World Bank report, Modi said in just 1213 years, 50 crore people have overcome poverty.Modi said the basic corporate tax rate has been reduced from 30 per cent in 2014 to 22 per cent, and individual income of up to ₹12 lakh a year is also tax-free.While the government has reduced the corporate tax, he asked if the industry has increased the strength of employees and raised their wages.He also emphasised that a country progresses when it respects its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers, and not by hurling abuses day-in and day-out.Taking a jibe at past regimes, Modi said the industry's experience with previous governments has been so bitter that he has to bear the consequences."This is not the old government. This is a government of friends. It knows how to honour friendship, and you are my true friends. So, without hesitation or reservation, please write to me openly about what still needs to be improved," the prime minister said.He asked the industry to make 'India First' the foundation of every long-term investment decision over the next 20 years.This will make the country self-reliant and also open up new opportunities for your business to grow, he added.

headline: Who was VS Babu? MLA who defeated MK Stalin in Tamil Nadu’s Kolathur constituency dies of cardiac arrest; aged 75
content: V S Babu, the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) legislator who defeated DMK president MK Stalin in the 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, died on Thursday, November 19, at the age of 75. His death followed more than two months in hospital, where he had been receiving treatment for a prolonged respiratory illness.VS Babu was admitted to MGM Healthcare in Chennai. According to the hospital, his condition deteriorated despite medical treatment and intensive care. He suffered a cardiac arrest at 2.14 pm on Thursday and was declared dead at 2.24 pm.His death comes months after he defeated Stalin in Kolathur, ending the DMK leader's hold on the constituency since 2011.VS Babu's political journey: From DMK district secretary to TVK legislatorBorn in 1951, Babu spent much of his political career in Tamil Nadu's Dravidian political circles. He began his journey with the DMK and eventually became the party's North Chennai district secretary, building a presence through local organisational work.His first major electoral victory came in the 2006 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections, when he contested from Purasawalkam on a DMK ticket. He won the seat and served as an MLA until 2011.Babu was also involved in the DMK's campaign in Kolathur when Stalin contested from the newly formed constituency for the first time in 2011. However, differences with the party leadership later led to his departure from the DMK.He joined the AIADMK in June 2016 before making another political move in February 2026, when he joined actor-turned-politician Vijay's TVK.How VS Babu defeated MK Stalin in the 2026 Tamil Nadu electionsTVK fielded Babu against Stalin in Kolathur in the 2026 Assembly elections. The constituency had been represented by Stalin since 2011, making the contest one of the closely watched battles in the state.Babu secured 82,997 votes, defeating then incumbent Tamil Nadu CM, MK Stalin, who received 74,202 votes. VS Babu's winning margin was 8,795 votes.VS Babu's victory was particularly notable given his earlier association with the DMK and his role in the constituency's political organisation.MK Stalin challenged VS Babu's Kolathur election victoryBabu's victory also faced a legal challenge from MK Stalin. In August 2026, the DMK president approached the Madras High Court, alleging irregularities in the post-election verification of electronic voting machines (EVMs).Stalin sought a complete count of Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) slips and verification of all 286 EVMs used in the constituency. He also asked the court to declare Babu's election invalid.However, the Madras High Court dismissed his petition on September 3, ruling that the challenge was not maintainable as a writ petition. It said the matter would have to be pursued through the prescribed election petition process. The court did not examine the merits of Stalin's allegations.Vijay, Stalin mourn VS Babu's deathTVK chief and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay expressed grief over Babu's death, describing it as an irreparable loss. He recalled the legislator's commitment to public service and his close connection with people.DMK president MK Stalin also expressed shock over the news. In a post on X, he said he was saddened by Babu's passing and extended his condolences to the legislator's family and party members.Tamil Nadu Minister Aadhav Arjuna also paid tribute, recalling Babu's friendly nature and concern for residents of North Chennai. VS Babu's death leaves Kolathur seat vacant after defeating MK Stalin TVL MLA VS Babu's death leaves the Kolathur Assembly constituency without an MLA, months after the seat witnessed one of the biggest electoral upsets in the 2026 Tamil Nadu elections. MK Stalin had represented Kolathur continuously since 2011, but lost the constituency to Babu by 8,795 votes in the 2026 polls. His death now leaves the future of the Kolathur seat in focus, with a by-election required to fill the vacancy.

headline: Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins Igass celebrations, urges families to preserve folk traditions
content: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami took part in Igass celebrations at his official residence, playing Bhailo as part of the traditional observances and urging people to preserve folk customs. The programme was held on the eve of the festival and featured folk songs, traditional dances and performances. The event brought together Rajya Sabha MP and BJP state president Mahendra Bhatt, Cabinet Minister Ganesh Joshi, several MLAs, public representatives and officials. Traditional attire, music and performances presented elements of Uttarakhand’s cultural heritage. Culture as social capital Greeting residents on Igass, Dhami described the festival as an expression of the state’s folk culture, faith, traditions and collective joy. He said such occasions connect people with their roots, while reinforcing cultural identity and social unity. Uttarakhand’s folk festivals, songs, dances, cuisine, clothing and customs shape its identity, he said. The practice of playing Bhailo, singing together and participating in traditional dances, he said, carried values of mutual affection, cooperation, brotherhood and community participation. His remarks placed the emphasis on the role of households and communities in sustaining cultural practices. He said the true identity of a society lay in its language, culture and traditions, and that customs needed to be practised at home. Dhami said modernisation made it important to familiarise children and young people with the significance of local festivals. He named Igass, Harela, Phool Dei, Ghee Sankranti and Uttarayani among the festivals to connect young people with their roots. Families, he said, should explain the historical, social and cultural meaning of festivals, and encourage children to take part in village celebrations, fairs and cultural programmes. Reaching beyond state borders Dhami also underlined the contribution of Uttarakhandis living elsewhere. He said their observance of traditional festivals helped sustain the state’s cultural identity and offered younger generations a link with their homeland and ancestral villages. He appealed to residents to continue respecting and celebrating their dialects, languages, folk music, dances and festivals wherever they lived. He said participation would help keep Uttarakhand’s heritage alive for future generations. The Chief Minister said the state government was working to preserve and promote folk arts, traditional fairs, regional languages and historical traditions. He described cultural heritage as a shared responsibility of government, families, individuals and generations. Dhami also urged people to encourage local folk artists and artisans and support traditional products during festivals. He said Uttarakhand’s folk culture carried values including respect for nature, hard work and harmony. Making these practices part of everyday life, rather than limiting them to festival gatherings, was necessary to pass the heritage on, he said.

headline: ‘Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted’: PM Modi's blunt message to India Inc at FICCI AGM | 10 key takeaways
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday, November 19, urged Indian businesses to move beyond the domestic market, improve product quality, reduce import dependence and expand their global footprint, calling on industry leaders to make India First the foundation of their long-term investment decisions.Addressing the 100th Annual General Meeting and Annual Convention of the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, PM Modi outlined opportunities across the pharmaceuticals, agriculture, food processing, engineering, steel and aluminium sectors.He also challenged businesses to translate the benefits of tax reforms into higher salaries and more employment, while invoking Mahatma Gandhi's message of Swadeshi and self-reliance.Here are the key takeaways from PM Modi's address:1. Don't take Indian consumers for granted; improve product qualityPM Modi urged businesses to stop treating India's large domestic market as an assured destination for products, stressing that Indian consumers deserve the same quality of goods as overseas buyers.He criticised the practice of selling products to Indian customers by describing them as "export quality"."Do not take 140 crore Indians for granted as an assured market where anything will sell. Even today, sellers tell customers 'this is export quality' to convince them it is good. What do you take our countrymen for? Do they not deserve good quality? This mindset must change; my countrymen deserve top quality," he said.He added that India's domestic market should serve as a launchpad for global competitiveness rather than become a comfort zone."Our domestic market must not become our comfort zone. It should give us the confidence to compete in global markets," PM Modi said.2. Make 'India First' the foundation of investment decisionsThe Prime Minister asked industry leaders to look beyond short-term business gains and prepare for emerging requirements in India and international markets.He called on businesses to prioritise national interests while making long-term investment decisions over the next two decades."In every long-term investment decision of yours for the next 20 years, make India First your foundation," he said.PM Modi said this approach would strengthen India's self-reliance while creating new opportunities for businesses.He also warned that companies needed to prepare for a world where resources were increasingly being used as strategic instruments."In this era of the weaponisation of resources, securing the nation's future becomes the responsibility of all of us," he said.3. Increase salaries and hiring after tax cutsPM Modi highlighted the government's tax reforms, including the reduction in the basic corporate tax rate and the income-tax exemption for earnings up to ₹12 lakh under the applicable provisions.However, he questioned whether companies had passed on the benefits of these measures through higher employee salaries and additional hiring."We brought the basic corporate tax rate down from 30% in 2014 to 22%, and today there is no income tax on earnings up to ₹12 lakh. Did you increase your employees' salaries or hire more staff?" he asked.He also highlighted improvements in tax administration, claiming that income-tax refunds that previously took several months were now generally processed within a week.GST reforms had also reduced taxes on several products, supporting consumer demand and benefiting businesses, he said.4. Reduce dependence on imported pharmaceutical ingredientsPM Modi urged India's pharmaceutical industry to reduce its dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), bulk drugs and drug intermediates.Despite being known as the "pharmacy of the world", India continues to import billions of dollars' worth of pharmaceutical ingredients every year, he said."India is called the 'pharmacy of the world,' yet it imports billions of dollars' worth of APIs, bulk drugs, and drug intermediates every year," he said.He asked pharmaceutical companies to identify ingredients that could be manufactured domestically and invest in new technologies and large-scale production facilities."In finished medicines, we have strength. Now we will have to build our capabilities in ingredients as well," Modi said.5. Export value-added products instead of raw materialsThe Prime Minister questioned why India continued to export raw materials while importing finished products, calling for greater domestic manufacturing and value addition."What kind of a country is this, and what kind of industrialists are we, if we export wheat and import bread?" he asked.He cited opportunities in the steel and aluminium industries, noting that India exports iron ore but imports finished steel, while also importing specialised aluminium alloys despite having substantial bauxite reserves.He urged companies to identify the grades of steel and aluminium products that India imports and develop the technology and manufacturing capabilities to produce them domestically.6. Invest more in agriculture and food processingPM Modi called on the corporate sector to increase investments in agriculture, food processing and procurement infrastructure to expand India's agricultural exports.He said India's share of global agricultural exports remained at around 2-2.5%, highlighting the considerable room for growth."I would urge you to increase your industry's investment in India's agricultural sector. Set up reliable procurement systems with specific overseas markets in mind, and develop products for which there is demand there, so that Indian products can become our calling card around the world," he said.He also highlighted the rise in processed food's share of India's agri-food exports from 13% to more than 20% over the past 12 years.Businesses, he said, should focus on value addition and develop products according to the requirements of specific international markets.7. Focus on hand tools, machinery and engineering exportsThe Prime Minister identified hand tools, power tools and machinery manufacturing as sectors where Indian companies could build a stronger global presence.He encouraged large companies to help smaller enterprises develop manufacturing capabilities that meet international quality and scale requirements.PM Modi also pointed to opportunities in manufacturing machinery for developing economies, particularly countries in the Global South.Packaging equipment, irrigation systems and factory-related machinery were among the areas where Indian businesses could explore export opportunities, he said.8. Use free trade agreements to expand global marketsPM Modi asked Indian industry leaders to take advantage of the Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) signed with several major economies.He said these agreements had opened new opportunities for Indian manufacturers and exporters, but questioned whether businesses had adequately prepared to exploit them."India has signed Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with several major economies; doors have opened for you. Have you planned to seize this opportunity? If you do not take advantage of all my hard work, who will?" he said.He urged companies to invest in overseas market research, understand consumer preferences and establish distribution networks to strengthen India's export presence.9. Take forward Mahatma Gandhi's message of SwadeshiMarking FICCI's 100th anniversary, PM Modi invoked Mahatma Gandhi's 1930 message of Swadeshi and self-reliance, saying Indian businesses needed to carry forward the same vision.He questioned why the country still needed to emphasise indigenous manufacturing and self-reliance nearly a century after Gandhi advocated the use of domestic products."Imagine, 100 years have passed, but in 1930, Gandhi left us with this message, and today, so many years later, I too have to say the same thing. Is this your success or your failure? Don't listen to me; at least you could have listened to Gandhi!" he said.He urged industry leaders to spread the message of Swadeshi and Atmanirbhar Bharat across the country.10. 'This is a government of friends': PM Modi invites industry suggestions Modi also urged businesses to move beyond any hesitation arising from their experiences with previous governments and openly communicate their concerns to the current administration. "Your experience with previous governments has been so bitter that I am having to bear the consequences. This is not the old government; this is a government of friends. It knows how to honour friendship, and you are my true friends," he said. He invited industry representatives to submit written suggestions on areas requiring further reforms, assuring them that the government was open to addressing their concerns. India has moved beyond 'Fragile Five', says PM Highlighting India's economic performance, PM Modi said the country had moved from being counted among the world's "Fragile Five" economies to becoming the fastest-growing major economy. He cited a recent World Bank report, saying around 500 million Indians had moved out of poverty over the past 12-13 years. He also highlighted merchandise exports of nearly $50 billion in October, describing it as the highest-ever monthly goods export figure. "Today, India stands as the world's fastest-growing major economy, with projected growth of around 7%. In October, India's goods exports reached nearly $50 billion, our highest-ever monthly goods export," he said. PM Modi added that international institutions, including Moody's Ratings, S&P Global Ratings, Fitch Ratings, the World Bank and the Asian Development Bank, had revised their growth projections for India upwards. Indian industry must focus on the next 20 years Concluding his message to industry leaders, Modi said FICCI's centenary was an opportunity to reflect on the contribution Indian businesses could make over the next two decades. He urged companies to prepare for future domestic and global demand instead of concentrating only on sectors that already offered established business opportunities. "Over its 100 years, FICCI has seen the country's industry achieve a great deal. Now is the time to decide what Indian industry can achieve in the next 20 years--how you can further increase your contribution to the journey of Viksit Bharat and Atmanirbhar Bharat," he said. "Developed India is not a slogan; it is a commitment," PM Modi added. (With PTI/ANI inputs)

headline: Don’t take Indians for granted: PM to corporates
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday took a dig at the corporate world, asking whether they hiked their employees’ salaries and created more jobs after the income tax concessions. He also cautioned the industry leaders not to take the 140 crore Indians for granted and to provide them with quality products and services.The jibe came after reports about massive retrenchments and salary cuts in the corporate world. “How much ever you give, their appetite is never satisfied,” Modi said in a pointed remark to the industry, adding that businesses needed to do more for their employees rather than expect the Government to shoulder the responsibility for growth.He also did not spare the Opposition and said, “No country can progress unless it respects its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers. A country cannot move forward by abusing them morning and evening.”Addressing the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) here, the Prime Minister said, “I have waived income tax on the `12 lakh bracket, but did you increase salaries or the number of employees? ‘Modi ji aap karo hum dekh lenge’, is this how things will function?” drawing laughter from the crowd.Modi said the Government had taken several steps to improve the business environment, including reducing the basic corporate tax rate from 30 per cent in 2014 to 22 per cent, simplifying tax return and refund processes and lowering GST rates on several products.“I know you won’t applaud. I know that very well, because your appetite is so enormous that no matter how much you are given, it is never enough,” he told industry leaders.He also cited the income-tax exemption for annual incomes of up to `12 lakh, saying the relief had boosted people’s purchasing power and should translate into greater demand and business expansion.He said a country could progress only by respecting its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers, and not by criticising them. “No country can progress unless it respects its farmers, small entrepreneurs, industries, wealth creators and taxpayers. A country cannot move forward by abusing them morning and evening,” he said.The PM also cautioned businesses against treating India’s large domestic market as an assured source of sales, saying companies must improve product quality and become globally competitive.“Do not consider the 140 crore Indians an assured market,” he said, urging industry to shed the mindset that whatever it produces will automatically find buyers in the domestic market.He criticised the practice of marketing products as “export quality” to Indian consumers, asking whether people in the country did not deserve the same quality as overseas customers. “My countrymen deserve quality,” he said.Modi urged Indian businesses to take advantage of the trade agreements signed by India with several countries, saying these had opened doors to major global markets.He described the agreements as a historic opportunity for Indian industry and asked businesses whether they had prepared plans to tap the new markets.Modi called on companies to invest in understanding the preferences and requirements of consumers across different regions, develop products suited to local markets, meet international standards and build distribution networks overseas.“Our domestic market should not be our comfort zone. It should give us the confidence to compete in global markets,” he said.Modi said the Government was willing to consider industry suggestions on further reforms and asked business leaders to share their requirements without hesitation.“This is not the government of the past. This is a friendly government. It knows how to honour friendship,” he said, inviting industry representatives to write to him about the changes they wanted.Modi urged industry to make ‘India First’ the foundation of its long-term investment decisions over the next 20 years, saying this would strengthen national self-reliance while opening new opportunities for businesses.He also called for greater domestic manufacturing of pharmaceutical ingredients, specialised steel and aluminium products, agricultural and processed foods, engineering tools and machinery to reduce import dependence and strengthen India’s export competitiveness.Modi recalled addressing a gathering of the income tax department in Gujarat in 2001-02. He had become Chief Minister of Gujarat then. “I did not understand much at the time; I had little knowledge and no experience either. But I delivered a speech there. This must have been around 2001-02, perhaps 25 years ago. All the senior officials of the Income Tax Department were present. I asked them: ‘When will you stop treating everyone as a thief? What kind of approach is this? You, too, work for the country. Are we the only ones who have taken it upon ourselves to serve the nation? You do your bit, and every citizen does theirs. Everyone deserves respect.’”

headline: Own MLAs accuse Telangana Congress govt of corruption in tenders, diversion of funds: KTR
content: Hyderabad: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president K T Rama Rao (KTR) on Thursday accused the Congress government of corruption, citing allegations made by Congress MLAs over commissions in government works, irregularities in tenders and diversion of funds.Speaking at a programme at Telangana Bhavan in Hyderabad, where leaders and workers from various parties in Bhupalpally joined the BRS, KTR alleged that government works were not being cleared without payment of 20 per cent commission.He referred to Jadcherla MLA Anirudh Reddy's remarks that works were not being executed without payment of commissions and Munugode MLA Komatireddy Rajgopal Reddy's allegations against Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy involving Rs 5 lakh crore, tender irregularities and scams.KTR said the allegations made by Congress legislators themselves raised questions about the functioning of the government. He claimed that some ruling party MLAs had approached the World Bank seeking funds for their constituencies.He also referred to Congress MLA Yennam Srinivas Reddy's reported remarks that funds meant for his constituency were being diverted to Kodangal. Rama Rao alleged that Congress legislators were being left with little to do beyond attending weddings and funerals.The BRS leader alleged that Revanth Reddy believed he could secure votes by distributing Rs 15,000 per voter using money obtained through corruption. He said the BRS would return to power after a year and recover money allegedly accumulated through corrupt practices by Congress leaders.Rama Rao accused the Congress government of misleading pension beneficiaries by announcing fresh pensions while removing existing beneficiaries from the rolls.He claimed that Telangana had 44.70 lakh pension beneficiaries during the previous BRS government. According to him, the Congress government had removed 1.50 lakh pensions in its first year, another 1.50 lakh in the second year and 1.70 lakh in the third year, taking the total number of deletions to 4.70 lakh.Against these deletions, the government had sanctioned only 4.63 lakh new pensions, leaving a difference of 7,000 beneficiaries, he claimed.KTR questioned why the pension budget had not increased if the government had expanded pension coverage. He accused the Congress of presenting replacement pensions as fresh benefits.Referring to the Congress election promise to increase pensions to Rs 4,000 within 100 days of assuming office, he said beneficiaries continued to receive Rs 2,000 despite three Decembers having passed.He said the previous BRS government had increased pensions from Rs 200 to Rs 2,000 and claimed that beneficiaries would have been receiving Rs 4,000 had the K. Chandrashekar Rao government continued in office.Rama Rao also criticised Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka over the Congress promise to implement six guarantees within 100 days. He recalled that Vikramarka had taken an oath at a Hanuman temple, supported by an affidavit, regarding implementation of the guarantees.He said Congress leaders had asked people to preserve guarantee cards like credit cards but had failed to implement their commitments despite nearly three years having passed.He said the previous BRS government had undertaken several development initiatives in Bhupalpally, including the establishment of a municipality, district headquarters and a medical college.He said Telangana had only five medical colleges at the time of state formation and claimed that the number had increased to 32 during the Chandrashekar Rao government's tenure, creating opportunities for thousands of students to pursue medical education. Rama Rao also criticised the Congress and BJP leadership in Telangana, accusing leaders of both parties of placing the interests of their national leadership above those of the state.He alleged that Chief Minister Revanth Reddy appeared subservient to Congress leaders from Delhi and referred to his conduct during Priyanka Gandhi's visit.He also criticised PCC president Mahesh Goud and minister Vivek Venkatswamy over their conduct during Rahul Gandhi's motorcycle ride in Hyderabad.Turning to the BJP, Rama Rao referred to state party leader Ramchander Rao touching Union home minister Amit Shah's feet during the latter's visit to Hyderabad. He questioned why senior leaders were displaying such deference to national leaders.He said the movement for Telangana statehood had been centred on self-respect and accused both national parties of compromising that principle.Rama Rao further alleged that funds meant for Telangana were being diverted to Delhi. He claimed that Revanth Reddy's continuation as Chief Minister depended on satisfying the Congress central leadership and described him as a renewal Chief Minister rather than a regular Chief Minister.The BRS working president said public dissatisfaction with the Congress government would strengthen his party in the coming days. He expressed confidence that the BRS would return to power under Chandrashekar Rao's leadership.

headline: Bangladesh: Arson attacks target homes of Yunus, ex-minister
content: Violence is not stopping, as suspected arson attacks targeting the ancestral home of former interim Government of Bangladesh Chief Adviser Professor Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram and the residence of former State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shahriar Alam in Rajshahi have raised fresh security concerns.In the latest incident, a fire broke out at Prof Yunus’s ancestral home, known as ‘Niribili’, in the Panchlaish residential area of Chattogram city at around 11:30 pm on Wednesday.According to police, the fire started in an unused section on the ground floor of the four-storey building. Police personnel stationed at the residence quickly brought the flames under control, preventing major damage and casualties.Chattogram Metropolitan Police Commissioner Hasan Mohammad Shawkat Ali said investigators recovered an empty bottle from the scene, which they suspect had contained a petrol-based flammable substance.He said preliminary findings indicated that unidentified individuals might have thrown a bottle containing the substance into the premises from outside. The commissioner also suspected possible involvement of individuals associated with a banned political party, although the allegation has yet to be independently established.Police are investigating the incident and working to identify and arrest those responsible.The affected section of the building had reportedly remained unused for around 10 to 15 years, with old furniture, clothes and documents stored inside. Families of two of Prof Yunus’s brothers live on the upper floors of the residence.Meanwhile, in a separate incident on Thursday, the house of former State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shahriar Alam was set on fire in Chaksinga village of Bagha upazila in Rajshahi.Officer-in-Charge of Bagha Police Station Serajul Haque said five to six unidentified individuals arrived on motorcycles at around 11 am, climbed over the boundary wall and entered the property before allegedly pouring petrol and setting the building ablaze.The fire quickly spread across part of the four-storey house. Residents rushed to the scene and managed to extinguish the flames by throwing water. No casualties were reported.A video circulated on social media showed flames burning inside the ground floor of the building.The two incidents, occurring within a short period, have intensified concerns over attacks on residences linked to prominent political figures.Police have yet to announce any arrests in connection with either incident. Investigations are underway to establish the motives behind the attacks and bring those responsible to justice.

headline: PM Modi pays tribute to Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary
content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday paid tribute to former prime minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, remembering the veteran Congress leader who served as India's first woman prime minister.In a post on social media platform X, Modi wrote, "Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary.".Indira Gandhi was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, now Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. She was the daughter of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, and became the country's first woman to hold the top constitutional executive office.She served as prime minister from 1966 to 1977 and returned to the position in January 1980, remaining in office until her assassination on October 31, 1984, in New Delhi..Several political leaders also remembered the former prime minister on the occasion.
