Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar paid tribute to Gandhi, describing her as the 'Iron Lady' and highlighting her contributions to India's political, economic and institutional development.In his message, Shivakumar recalled initiatives associated with her tenure, including strengthening agricultural production, expanding banking access and supporting the country's space and nuclear programmes..Gandhi remains one of the most consequential and controversial figures in India's post-Independence political history. Her tenure witnessed significant developments in the country's domestic and foreign policy, including the nationalisation of major banks in 1969 and the 1971 India-Pakistan war, which led to the creation of Bangladesh.She was assassinated by two of her bodyguards on October 31, 1984, months after the Indian Army's Operation Bluestar at the Golden Temple in Amritsar.Her birth anniversary is also observed as National Integration Day, commemorating her contributions to the country.(With inputs from agencies)

headline: How GTA VI launch gave PM Modi, Assam CM a pitch & Congress a chance to spar
content: Guwahati/New Delhi, Nov 19: As gamers around the world explore the virtual streets of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI), Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma has suggested that Guwahati, too, is gearing up for its own set of upgrades, bonus levels and perhaps a little action.“GTA VI may be launching today, but Guwahati is busy unlocking its own upgrades and bonus levels. And trust us, it's going to be epic,” Sarma posted on social media on Thursday, sharing a GTA-inspired visual of Guwahati featuring the Brahmaputra, the city's iconic bridge, a helicopter and a dramatic sunset.GTA VI may be launching today, but Guwahati is busy unlocking its own upgrades and bonus levels. And trust us it's going to be epic. https://t.co/P4Qhgeb3n3— Himanta Biswa Sarma (@himantabiswa) November 19, 2026 The post added an Assam twist to the global GTA VI buzz, which has also spilled into Indian politics after Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the popular video game franchise to showcase what he described as India's development journey over the years. Modi, in a social media post on Thursday, drew a comparison between Grand Theft Auto V, released in 2013, and GTA VI, released globally on Thursday, using the gap between the two games to highlight changes in India's development indicators. GTA V was released in September 2013, months before Modi became prime minister in May 2014.India is playing a whole new game! https://t.co/CMkMbK6vII— Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) November 19, 2026 Titled “Between GTA 5 and 6, here's how India upgraded”, the post featured 10 slides highlighting changes across various development indicators. From being described as one of the “Fragile Five” economies to becoming the world's fastest-growing major economy, Modi presented a series of before-and-after comparisons to underline what he described as India's progress. Among the figures highlighted were India's solar power capacity, which he said had risen from 2.82 GW to 175 GW, and railway electrification, which increased from 20 per cent to 99.6 per cent. He also pointed to a decline in extreme poverty from 27% to 2.6%, an increase in sanitation coverage from 39 per cent to 100 per cent, and a fall in the cost of 1 GB of internet data from Rs 308 to Rs 7.51. The Prime Minister also highlighted the growth of India's space sector, saying the number of space startups had risen from one to 440. “India is playing a whole new game,” Modi wrote, using the gaming franchise as a metaphor for the country's transformation. But the political Opposition was not quite ready to play along. Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh took a swipe at the Prime Minister's choice of analogy, suggesting that the gaming reference was particularly ironic. “The PM, in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth, has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media,” Ramesh said.The PM in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media. Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate.— Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) November 19, 2026 “Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate,” he added in a social media post. The exchange has given the launch of GTA VI an unexpected political side quest, with the ruling establishment using the game's popularity to communicate its development narrative and the Opposition turning the same reference into a political punchline. Developed and published by Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI is the latest instalment in the popular action-adventure franchise, following GTA V, which was released in 2013. The game began its global rollout on Thursday, ending a 13-year wait for the latest mainline entry in the series.With inputs from PTI

headline: Tripura CM predicts BJP sweep of all 51 Agartala civic awards
content: Agartala, Nov 19: Tripura Chief Minister Manik Saha on Thursday expressed confidence that the BJP would sweep all 51 wards of the Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) in the November 27 civic elections, claiming that voters were satisfied with the civic body's performance over the past five years.Campaigning for the polls, Saha said the BJP was reaching out to voters with its development agenda and receiving an encouraging response across the city."We are reaching out to each voter with the message of development and receiving positive feedback for the good work done by the civic body. Wherever we go, people are welcoming us with smiling faces. It shows that voters are happy," he told reporters.The Chief Minister highlighted the improvements made in Agartala since the BJP took charge of the municipal corporation, particularly in drinking water supply, road infrastructure and urban amenities."When the BJP assumed office at the AMC, drinking water coverage was merely 3 per cent. It has now increased to 86 per cent. The corporation has also developed roads, improved street lighting and redeveloped several lakes, thereby improving the quality of life," he said.The BJP had won all 51 wards in the 2021 AMC elections, defeating the CPI(M)-led Left Front and the Congress.Agriculture Minister Ratan Lal Nath, who is overseeing the BJP's election strategy for the municipal polls, also predicted a decisive victory for the party, dismissing the electoral prospects of the opposition."We don't think the CPI(M) will secure even an average of 1,000 votes in any AMC ward, while the Congress is unlikely to cross 500 votes in any ward," Nath said.Responding to questions about the BJP's decision to deny a ticket to incumbent mayor Dipak Majumder, Nath said the party was following its 'one leader, one post' principle by not fielding sitting MLAs in the civic elections.Praising Majumder's tenure, Nath described him as the most successful mayor since the establishment of the civic body and said the decision should not be viewed as a reflection of his performance."Our mayor is unparalleled when it comes to performance. The party decided not to give any MLA a ticket to contest the civic elections. Who knows, he may get a more important portfolio in the future. As a mayor, Dipak Majumder has been the most successful since the civic body came into existence," he said.Elections to Tripura's civic bodies, including the Agartala Municipal Corporation, are scheduled for November 27, while counting of votes will take place on December 2.PTI

headline: Assam Cabinet clears 6 new municipal boards, startup policy & land rule changes
content: Guwahati, Nov 19: Strengthening urban governance, the Assam Cabinet on Thursday approved the creation of six new municipal boards, besides expansion and ward delimitation in 23 existing urban local bodies.Addressing a press conference at Assam Bhawan in New Delhi after the Cabinet meeting, Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the new municipal boards would also help promote entrepreneurship in educational institutions and address land-related concerns. “We have approved six new municipal boards: Laluk Municipal Board and Harmoti-Bandarduwa Municipal Board; Majuli Municipal Board in Majuli; Udharbond Municipal Board in Cachar; and Mirza Municipal Board and Bijoynagar Municipal Board in Kamrup,” he said. The Cabinet also approved the expansion of areas and ward delimitation in 23 existing Urban Local Bodies. “The decisions are part of the state government’s efforts to strengthen the functioning of urban local bodies and improve urban governance,” Sarma said.Innovation & startup policy for higher education In another significant decision, the Cabinet approved the “Innovation and Startup Policy in Higher Educational Institutions” to encourage entrepreneurship and innovation across the state. Sarma said the policy would facilitate the development of innovation and startup incubation centres in colleges and universities, while strengthening the broader ecosystem required to support emerging entrepreneurs. The initiative is expected to provide institutional support to students and young innovators seeking to develop entrepreneurial ideas into viable ventures.New definition of urban areas for land benefits The Cabinet also approved decisions concerning land-related issues discussed during recent meetings with representatives of different indigenous communities of Assam. Under the revised approach, the government has decided to consider areas within one kilometre of a town's boundary as urban for the purpose of extending the relevant benefits under the Basundhara scheme, instead of treating the entire area covered by a town's master plan as urban. Sarma said areas falling within an urban master plan but beyond the one-kilometre limit would continue to be treated as rural. "We have decided that only the town area and the one-kilometre belt beyond its boundary will be considered urban. The remaining areas, even if they fall under the urban master plan, will be treated as villages. This relaxation will not apply to Kamrup Metropolitan and Kamrup districts," he said.Higher honorariums for panchayat representatives The Cabinet also approved an increase in the monthly honorariums of elected representatives at the Zila Parishad, Anchalik Panchayat and Gaon Panchayat levels. At the Zila Parishad level, the monthly honorarium of presidents has been increased from Rs 10,000 to Rs 15,000, while vice-presidents will now receive Rs 10,000 instead of Rs 7,500. Members will receive Rs 5,500, up from Rs 4,000. For Anchalik Panchayats, presidents will receive Rs 10,000 instead of Rs 7,500, while the honorarium of vice-presidents has been raised from Rs 5,000 to Rs 7,000. Members will now receive Rs 6,000, compared to the earlier Rs 3,000. At the Gaon Panchayat level, presidents will receive Rs 6,500 instead of Rs 5,000, while vice-presidents will get Rs 4,000, up from Rs 3,000. The honorarium of members has been increased from Rs 2,000 to Rs 2,600. The revised honorariums are aimed at enhancing financial support for elected representatives involved in grassroots governance.Land pattas for ICAR and Army The Cabinet also approved the allotment of land-related rights for two institutions. At Gogamukh, 1,568 bighas of land under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) will be granted miyadi patta. In Sonitpur district, 75 bighas of land at Missamari will be allotted to the Army.Seven-day window for Moran, Motok council polls The Cabinet also decided to reduce the period for filing claims and objections in the electoral process for the Moran and Motok Autonomous Councils from 15 days to seven days, paving the way for the elections to be held within December. "Normally, the claims and objections period is 15 days. However, since there was a demand to hold the elections this year, we have reduced it to seven days so that the Moran and Motok Autonomous Council elections can be conducted within December," Sarma said.

headline: Congress leaders pay tribute to Indira Gandhi on 109th birth anniversary
content: New Delhi, Nov 19: Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge and Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) Chairperson Sonia Gandhi on Thursday paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her 109th birth anniversary at Shakti Sthal in the national capital.Kharge also took to the social media platform X and paid homage to the former Prime Minister, describing her as India's 'Iron Lady' and a symbol of courage, struggle and strong leadership."With deepest reverence on the birth anniversary of India's 'Iron Lady' and former Prime Minister, Smt. Indira Gandhi, a symbol of indomitable courage, struggle and strong leadership. She sacrificed her life to protect the country's unity, integrity and sovereignty. Her dedication to the nation, her contributions, her unwavering resolve and her decisive leadership will forever inspire us," he wrote in Hindi.Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar also paid tribute to Indira Gandhi and recalled her contributions to the country's development.In a post on X, CM Shivakumar said her tenure witnessed significant political, economic and institutional developments.He highlighted her role in strengthening agricultural production, expanding access to banking services and supporting India's space and nuclear programmes."As we remember her journey in public life, we also recognise the mark she left on India's political landscape and its development trajectory. Her contributions remain an important part of India's post-independence history, and her memory will continue to be remembered with respect," he said.Indira Gandhi, popularly known as the 'Iron Lady of India', was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, into a Kashmiri Pandit family. She was the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, and Kamala Nehru.She served as the Prime Minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from January 1980 until her assassination in 1984. She became a member of the Rajya Sabha in August 1964 and served until February 1967. Subsequently, she was elected to the Lok Sabha and remained a member during its fourth, fifth and sixth terms.Indira Gandhi was India's second-longest-serving Prime Minister after her father, Jawaharlal Nehru. She was known for several significant economic and social measures, including the nationalisation of banks and the abolition of privy purses granted to former princely states.One of the most defining moments of her tenure was her leadership during the 1971 India-Pakistan war, which resulted in the creation of Bangladesh. Her role in the conflict established her reputation as a decisive leader with strong political resolve.National Integration Day is observed annually on November 19 to mark her birth anniversary and commemorate her contributions to national unity and integration.Throughout her political career, Gandhi emphasised the importance of bringing together people from diverse regions, cultures and communities under a common national identity. Her policies and political approach focused on strengthening India's unity and advancing its development.Indira Gandhi was assassinated on October 31, 1984, by two of her bodyguards, months after she ordered Operation Bluestar. The military operation was launched to flush out armed separatists who had taken shelter inside the Golden Temple in Amritsar, one of Sikhism's holiest shrines.(IANS)

headline: CM Sarma meets Sitharaman, discusses Assam’s development goals & Centre's support
content: Guwahati, Nov 19: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma met Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman in New Delhi on Thursday and discussed key issues related to the state’s development, including its economic indicators and Centre’s support for Assam’s growth.According to the Chief Minister’s Office, the meeting also covered India’s growing role amid global economic turbulence and the Centre’s support for Assam’s development journey. Sarma said Sitharaman reaffirmed the Centre’s full support for helping Assam achieve its development goals. “It is always a privilege to work with Smt @nsitharaman Ji, whose approachability and pragmatism have greatly served Assam’s growth. India’s continued outperformance of its global peers, despite strong headwinds, is a testament to her leadership,” Sarma said in a social media post. “In today’s meeting, the Hon’ble Finance Minister reaffirmed the Government of India’s full support in propelling Assam towards its development goals,” he added.The meeting comes around two months after Sarma and Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad K Sangma met Sitharaman in New Delhi to seek a fresh push for Externally Aided Projects (EAPs) in the two northeastern states.CM Dr @himantabiswa called on Union Finance Minister Smt @nsitharaman in New Delhi today to discuss key matters concerning Assam’s development. He appreciated her continued support and pragmatic approach towards Assam’s growth. The Finance Minister reaffirmed the Central Government’s full support in helping Assam achieve its development goals.— Chief Minister Assam (@CMOfficeAssam) November 19, 2026 The meeting, held at Kartavya Bhawan, focused on increasing capital expenditure in the Northeast and creating new investment channels for physical and social infrastructure through EAPs.Sarma had said Sitharaman responded positively to the proposals and assured the two chief ministers of a renewed push by the Centre to advance the region’s development agenda. Sitharaman, meanwhile, chaired the seventh pre-Budget consultation with experts from the infrastructure, energy and sustainability sectors in New Delhi on Thursday as part of preparations for the Union Budget 2027-28. The Finance Ministry said in a social media post that the consultation was held with experts from the three sectors in connection with the forthcoming Budget. The Union Budget 2027-28 is expected to be presented on February 1, 2027. The Economic Survey, which assesses the country’s economic performance and outlook, is likely to be tabled on January 29 or January 31, 2027. With inputs from agencies

headline: Jackie Shroff takes part in Yamuna cleanup drive with Delhi CM
content: Mumbai, Nov 19: Actor Jackie Shroff joined Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta for a post-Chhath Puja cleanliness drive aimed at promoting the cleanliness and conservation of the Yamuna river.The ‘Karma’ actor, along with Esha Gupta and singer Stebin Ben, participated in the campaign at Munak Nehar in Shalimar Bagh, where they were seen taking part in the cleaning activity. In the video, Jackie Shroff was seen wearing gloves as he actively participated in the cleaning drive, picking up waste and collecting it before disposing of it in a designated area.During the drive, Jackie highlighted the importance of protecting rivers and water bodies, urging people to be mindful of how they dispose of waste. He stressed that keeping rivers clean was a collective responsibility and called on citizens to take an active role in preserving them for future generations.Speaking about the initiative, the ‘Border’ actor said, “Cleaning the water and cleaning the river, I think it is everyone's duty. Not for us, but for our children, the whole gang behind us. We had left. Now what we are leaving is in your hands. It is our duty to clean every river.”He further appealed to people not to throw waste into rivers, particularly those considered sacred and worshipped by devotees."Keeping the water clean and cleaning the Yamuna is everyone's responsibility. It is our duty to keep every river clean. We should not dump our waste at the feet of the very goddesses we worship. Please be careful. We consider these rivers goddesses and worship them, don't we?" he added.Addressing the media, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the initiative was part of a broader campaign aimed at enhancing cleanliness and expanding green spaces across Delhi. “This is not just about the Munak Canal; it is about all of Delhi, our mother Yamuna, the cleanliness of the city, and making the city green.”(IANS)

headline: AAP expects over 1 lakh people at Moga Foundation Day rally to kick-start 2027 poll campaign
content: CHANDIGARH: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) expects more than one lakh people to attend its Foundation Day rally in Moga on November 26, with the event set to formally kick-start the party's campaign for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.The rally, spread across approximately 116 acres, will be attended by AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann and the party's senior leadership, Punjab Working President Amansher Singh Shery Kalsi and state Media In-charge Baltej Pannu said.Kalsi reviewed the preparations for the rally and said party volunteers, workers, leaders and supporters from across Punjab were expected to attend the gathering.He said the rally would send a strong political message to opposition parties and demonstrate the public support the AAP government had earned through its five years in power in Punjab. He added that people from across the state would participate in large numbers, reflecting their faith in the government's work.Explaining the choice of Moga as the venue, Kalsi said the party leadership and its MLAs had collectively decided that the district's central location and accessibility for people from Majha, Doaba, Malwa and border areas made it the most suitable place for the rally.He said the gathering would be among the biggest political rallies in Punjab's history and that its significance would be further enhanced by being held on the party's Foundation Day..Meanwhile, AAP Punjab General Secretary and Media In-charge Baltej Pannu said arrangements had been made across the 116-acre venue, with plans to expand it further if required. He said facilities such as washrooms, food and drinking water would be available to attendees.Pannu said separate parking arrangements had been made on both sides of the venue to prevent traffic congestion. Vehicles and buses arriving from the Ludhiana side would be directed to a designated parking area, while a larger parking facility had been arranged on the Moga side to accommodate the expected influx of attendees.To facilitate women and elderly people, buses and e-rickshaws would be deployed to ferry attendees from designated drop-off points and parking areas to the rally venue. The arrangements were aimed at ensuring that they did not have to walk long distances to reach the pandal.Pannu said the party had paid special attention to logistical arrangements to ensure a smooth and comfortable experience for those attending the rally..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Green Castle Smart School, Chandigarh, organises educational visit to gurdwara
content: Green Castle Smart School, Chandigarh, organised an educational visit to a gurdwara for students of the junior section to familiarise them with Sikh culture, traditions and religious values. During the visit, the students paid obeisance, listened to the Mool Mantar and learnt about the significance of covering their heads, maintaining cleanliness, offering prayers and receiving karah prasad. The teachers explained the various rituals and the importance of the gurdwara, helping the children understand the values of equality, humility, devotion and selfless service (Seva). The Principal also encouraged students to respect all religions and appreciate India's rich cultural diversity.

headline: Panjab University improves its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research
content: CHANDIGARH Chandigarh-based Panjab University (PU) has improved its global standing in interdisciplinary scientific research, climbing 24 places to secure the joint 150th position in the Times Higher Education (THE) Interdisciplinary Science Rankings 2027. The University’s overall score has increased to 55.0 from 52.8 in 2026 and 48.6 in 2025. In a statement on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), Vice-Chancellor Meenakshi Goyal said, “This improvement in Panjab University’s global standing reflects our continued commitment to strengthening interdisciplinary research and academic collaboration. It is the outcome of the collective efforts of our faculty, researchers, students, and staff. We will continue to build an enabling research ecosystem that encourages collaboration across disciplines, supports innovation, and addresses complex societal challenges aimed at Viksit Bharat through knowledge and research.” The 2027 edition of the rankings, produced by Times Higher Education in association with Schmidt Science Fellows, assessed 1,058 institutions across 102 countries and territories, compared with 911 institutions in the 2026 edition. A total of 565 Asian institutions were ranked, up from 478 last year. The Interdisciplinary Science Rankings assess universities’ contributions and commitment to research that brings together knowledge and methods from different academic disciplines to address complex challenges. The rankings cover collaborations involving multiple scientific disciplines as well as research combining scientific disciplines with areas such as the social sciences, education, psychology, law, economics, and clinical and health studies.

headline: Environment Ministry orders zero tolerance on waste burning, strict action against Delhi-NCR pollution violators
content: Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav on Thursday directed civic bodies in Delhi-NCR to take strict penal action against those found burning municipal waste, dry leaves and biomass, and ensure daily monitoring of pollution control measures as part of their winter action plans.Chairing a review meeting virtually from Antalya, Turkiye, where he is to lead India at COP 31, with municipal bodies of Delhi, Ghaziabad, Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad, Yadav called for accountability of ward-level officials, time-bound enforcement and a zero-tolerance approach towards violations.He directed municipal corporations to set up Quick Response Teams in every ward to address complaints within hours and fix responsibility for enforcement failures. He also called for faster processing of daily municipal waste and accelerated clearance of legacy waste at Delhi's Bhalswa and Okhla dumpsites.On dust pollution, the Minister asked civic bodies to expedite road repairs, increase the deployment of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines and operate them in double shifts during winter. GPS-enabled monitoring and supervision through Integrated Command and Control Centres were also stressed to ensure regular removal of roadside dust, silt and construction debris.Directing strict compliance with dust-control norms at construction and demolition sites, Yadav called for operationalising wheel-washing facilities, regular inspections and closure of seriously non-compliant sites. The target, he said, should be to ensure 'No Visible Dust' around construction sites.He also asked civic bodies to prepare hotspot-specific action plans, appoint dedicated nodal officers and strictly implement all measures under the prevailing stage of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).The Minister called for regular ward-level reviews by mayors and dedicated WhatsApp groups with nodal officers to ensure time-bound grievance redressal. Complaints, he said, should be closed only after physical verification and resolution.Yadav also asked civic bodies to replicate successful initiatives across NCR, including the Municipal Corporation of Delhi's Malba App, Faridabad's Pothole Ambulance and Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam's Construction and Demolition waste portal.Collectors were directed to review municipal performance and take corrective action against lagging bodies. The Environment and Housing and Urban Affairs Ministries, CAQM and CPCB were also asked to monitor the implementation of pollution-control directions.

headline: Alleged Form 7 misuse in Delhi SIR: Supreme Court asks EC to verify claims, take remedial measures
content: <p>New Delhi: The <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/supreme-court">Supreme Court</a> on Thursday directed the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/election-commission">Election Commission</a> of India and the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer to verify a complaint by <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/congress">Congress</a> leader Ali Mehdi alleging fraudulent Form 7 applications seeking deletion of voters in the Mustafabad constituency during the <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/special-intensive-revision">Special Intensive Revision</a> (SIR) process.</p><p>A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana disposed of Mehdi’s writ petition without commenting on the merits. </p><p>The court ordered the authorities to examine the allegations and take necessary remedial steps strictly in accordance with law if they are found true.</p><p>The petition relied on a news reports, claiming that most booth-level agents in whose names the Form 7 applications were filed had denied signing them. </p><p>The reports further stated that several voters listed as dead or shifted were alive and residing at the addresses on record. </p><p>Mehdi contended that the applications were not filed by genuine objectors and targeted legitimate electors.</p>.Supreme Court to hear marital rape pleas for final hearing in December.<p>According to the petitioner, 28 electors against whom deletion applications were filed were found living at their given addresses. His counsel told the court that of the 37 Form 7s examined, 36 turned out to be false.</p><p>During the hearing, the bench observed that the Election Commission has no control over booth-level agents, who are appointed by political parties. </p><p>“If a booth-level agent makes a fraudulent application, the Election Commission can blacklist him. Beyond that, they have no control,” Justice Bagchi said.</p><p>Mehdi’s counsel pointed out that in the Uttar Pradesh Special Intensive Revision, the court had earlier asked the Commission to act against bulk filing of fake Form 7s. He also submitted that the police had refused to register an FIR on his complaint. </p><p>The bench advised him to approach the magistrate for registration of the case.</p><p>Noting that the petitioner had already submitted representations to the police, the Election Commission and the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer, the court declined to examine the allegations on merits. </p><p>“Since the petitioner has already submitted a representation, we dispose of the writ petition, without expressing any opinion, with a direction to the authorities to verify the allegation and take necessary remedial measures strictly in accordance with law,” the bench said.</p>

headline: Aadhaar card by itself not proof of date of birth: Delhi High Court
content: <p>New Delhi: The <a href="https://www.deccanherald.com/tags/delhi-high-court">Delhi High Court</a> has held that Aadhaar card is not, by itself, a proof of date of birth.</p>.<p>The court was dealing with a petition concerning a dispute between the date of birth of a workman who was allegedly illegally retrenched by her employer in 2017.</p>.Delhi High Court seeks ED, SFIO's stand on Tina Ambani's plea to disclose look-out circular.<p>In a judgement passed on November 13, Justice Manoj Kumar Ohri stated that the law on Aadhaar only recognises an Aadhaar number as "proof of identity", and as informed in an office memorandum issued by the UIDAI in 2018, the date of birth in the Aadhaar card is recorded based on documents or the self-declaration furnished by the cardholder.</p>.<p>While the employer in this case contended that the workman had attained the age of superannuation - i.e., 58 years - based on the May 20, 1959 date of birth in her Aadhaar card, the respondent workman claimed that her date of birth had to be determined on the basis of the Employees' State Insurance Corporation record, which had 1960 as the year of birth.</p>.<p>Agreeing with the workman that she was yet to attain the age of superannuation in 2017, the court stated that her Aadhaar card was not supported by any independent document on record, and it was admittedly received by the management merely two months before her services were brought to an end.</p>.<p>"The case of the management, thus, rests solely upon Ex. WW1/7 (Aadhaar). However, an Aadhaar card is not, by itself, proof of date of birth," the court held.</p>.<p>"The Office Memorandum dated 20.12.2018 issued by UIDAI, which has been placed on record by the workwoman, clarifies the said position. It records that UIDAI enters the date of birth on the basis of the documents or the self-declaration furnished by the card holder. It further records that the Aadhaar Act, 2016 recognises an Aadhaar number as proof of identity, but does not mention that it can be accepted as proof of date of birth," it observed.</p>.Delhi High Court gives 3 weeks to Arvind Kejriwal, other Aam Aadmi Party leaders to respond to criminal contempt case.<p>The court concluded that since the ESIC record showed her date of birth as May 20, 1960, the management could not later rely on a different date in an Aadhaar card to end her services a year earlier.</p>.<p>The court dismissed the management's petition against the labour court's ruling in favour of the workman and ruled that the termination of her services without compliance with the Industrial Disputes Act was rightly held to be illegal. </p>

headline: Supreme Court Directs EC to Verify False Voter Deletion Claims in Delhi’s Mustafabad
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Election Commission (EC) to verify allegations of fraudulent applications seeking the deletion of voters' names from electoral rolls in Delhi's Mustafabad Assembly constituency and take remedial measures in accordance with law.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V. Mohana issued the direction while hearing a petition alleging that false Form 7 applications were filed during the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Mustafabad. Form 7 is used to raise objections to the inclusion of names or seek the deletion of entries from electoral rolls.The petition cited news reports alleging that applications seeking deletion of voters' names had been filed in the names of certain booth-level agents (BLAs), who subsequently denied having submitted them.The petitioner's counsel told the court that complaints had been lodged with the police and representations submitted to the EC and Delhi's chief electoral officer (CEO).He said some voters whose names were sought to be deleted on the grounds that they had died or shifted residence were alive and continued to live at the same addresses."Let your representation be looked into by the authorities," the court said.The bench observed that the EC had no control over BLAs, who were appointed by political parties.Disposing of the petition without expressing any opinion on its merits, the court directed the authorities to examine the allegations and take necessary remedial measures strictly in accordance with law.On October 29, the EC revised the SIR schedule for five states and Delhi following requests from the respective CEOs.In Delhi, the deadline for filing claims and objections was extended from October 30 to November 25. The deadline for their disposal was shifted from November 30 to December 15, while the final electoral roll is scheduled for publication on December 22.The EC had published the draft rolls on August 31, reporting that approximately 47 lakh names had been omitted from the pre-revision electorate of about 1.45 crore in the national capital.

headline: Union Environment Minister directs Delhi-NCR Civic Bodies to adopt Zero-tolerance Approach towards Air Pollution Violations; Calls for Strict Penal Action against Defaulters
content:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change (EFCC), Shri Bhupender Yadav, today chaired a review meeting virtually from Antalya (Türkiye), with the civic bodies of Delhi, Ghaziabad, Noida, Gurugram and Faridabad to assess preparedness and implementation of their Winter Action Plans for control of air pollution in Delhi-NCR. Emphasising that the current winter period demands visible and sustained action on the ground, the Minister requested the concerned public representatives and officials to ensure strict enforcement, daily monitoring and clear accountability at every level. He stressed that governance should increasingly be citizen-centric and facilitative, while ensuring that citizens are not subjected to unnecessary panic while taking pollution control measures.

The meeting was attended by Union Minister of State (MoEFCC), Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh; Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Narendra Bhooshan; Chairperson (CAQM), Shri Rajesh Verma; Secretary (Department of Capital Development, MoHUA), Smt. D. Thara; Director General and Special Secretary (MoEFCC), Shri Santosh Tewari; Additional Secretary (MoEFCC) and Chairperson (CPCB), Dr. Amandeep Garg; Mayors and Commissioners of the respective Municipal Corporations, along with CEO Noida Authority and senior officials of respective State Governments. Shri Tarun Pithode, Member Secretary, CAQM, presented the progress made by respective NCR cities, while the Chairperson, CAQM, gave an overview of the on-ground implementation of their action plans and measures yet to be taken on different fronts.

Taking a strong stance against violations, Shri Yadav directed Municipal Corporations to adopt a zero-tolerance approach towards open burning of municipal waste, dry leaves and biomass, and ensure prompt penal action against violators. He called for operationalising Quick Response Teams in every ward to respond to complaints within hours, and fixing accountability of concerned officers for enforcement failures. He also called for immediate corrective measures for complete processing daily waste generated and time-bound accelerated legacy waste remediation, particularly at Bhalswa and Okhla dumpsites. Stressing the need for coordinated and decentralised governance, the Minister called for regular ward-level reviews by Mayors and dedicated WhatsApp groups with designated nodal officers for time-bound grievance redressal. He urged civic bodies to learn from and replicate successful initiatives across NCR, including MC Delhi's Malba App, MC Faridabad's Pothole Ambulance, MC Gurugram's survey-based identification of sanitation workers and Ghaziabad Nagar Nigam's shareable Construction and Demolition (C&D) waste portal.

On road dust management, Shri Yadav directed civic bodies to expedite road repairs, augment the capacity of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) on a war footing and ensure their full utilisation, including double-shift operations during winter. He called for GPS-enabled monitoring, ICCC-based supervision and daily removal of roadside dust, silt and construction debris. The Minister also stressed the need for advance planning of road development and dust mitigation measures in Gurugram, including greening of identified open spaces to address PM10 pollution. He directed strict compliance with dust mitigation norms at C&D sites, operationalisation of wheel-washing facilities and regular inspections, with stringent enforcement action, including closure of seriously non-compliant sites. The objective, he emphasised, must be to ensure 'No Visible Dust' in and around construction sites. The Minister further called for ensuring enhanced awareness about Solid Waste Management Rules, with proactive identification of bulk waste generators, as demonstrated by Delhi.

Reviewing hotspot mitigation and GRAP implementation, Shri Yadav directed civic bodies to assign dedicated nodal officers and prepare hotspot-specific action plans, which should be regularly reviewed by Mayors and the designated officers. He called for strict implementation of all measures applicable under the prevailing stage of GRAP, without exception. Emphasising institutional accountability, the Minister directed Collectors to regularly review the performance of municipalities and take corrective action against lagging bodies. He further called upon the Secretaries of MoEFCC and MoHUA, besides Chairpersons of the CAQM and CPCB, to review the performance of respective Municipal Corporations and municipalities across NCR cities to ensure effective implementation of the directions on the ground.

Stressing that accountability must translate into measurable outcomes, the Minister requested the concerned officials to monitor public grievances in real time and close complaints only after physical verification and resolution. He also called for intensive public awareness campaigns involving concerned stakeholders. Emphasising the need for sustained efforts throughout the winter season, Shri Yadav said every ward must demonstrate visible action every day, backed by strict enforcement, continuous monitoring, citizen participation and accountability.

headline: 13 Delhi railway stations set for upgrade: CM Rekha Gupta
content: NEW DELHI Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Wednesday said that 13 railway stations in Delhi are being redeveloped under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme as part of the ₹2,711 crore allocated for railway development in the Capital. “The allocation for expanding and modernising railway facilities in Delhi reflects the Centre’s commitment to modernising the Capital’s infrastructure and improving public amenities through the joint efforts of the Central and Delhi governments,” Ms. Gupta said. She added that the financial support was an important step towards strengthening Delhi’s railway infrastructure and providing better facilities to millions of passengers. The stations include New Delhi, Old Delhi, Hazrat Nizamuddin, Anand Vihar Terminal, Delhi Cantt, Delhi Sarai Rohilla, Delhi Shahdara, Narela, Safdarjung, Bijwasan, Sabzi Mandi, Tilak Bridge and Adarsh Nagar Delhi. Passenger amenities The redevelopment includes improved entry and exit arrangements, modernised station buildings, waiting rooms, seating arrangements, toilets, drinking water facilities, platform shelters, foot overbridges, lifts and escalators, a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office said. The work also covers parking facilities, accessibility for persons with disabilities, improved passenger information systems and better connectivity to both sides of the city. Ms. Gupta said the construction of a holding area on the Ajmeri Gate side of New Delhi Railway Station had been completed. Further work at the station, including the foundation for a double basement and an elevated road, has begun. “At Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station, the second entry point on the Sarai Kale Khan side is being redeveloped. At Delhi Cantt Station, a new station building, arrival and departure concourses, an elevated road, platform improvements and other facilities are being developed,” Ms. Gupta said. Vande Bharat service Ms. Gupta also said the recent launch of the New Delhi-Varanasi Vande Bharat Sleeper train would make travel between Delhi and major cities in Uttar Pradesh more convenient, as part of efforts to strengthen the Capital’s rail network. The train will reach New Delhi via Varanasi, Prayagraj, Kanpur, Aligarh and Ghaziabad. Equipped with modern facilities, it features automatic doors, the Kavach safety system and comfortable berths. The service would also encourage tourism, business, religious travel and regional connectivity, she added.

headline: 2 friends, 1 mystery: Drug mafia angle raised in Himachal girls’ deaths
content: Days after the bodies of two minor girls were recovered from a stream in Himachal Pradesh’s Bilaspur district, a BJP MLA on Thursday hinted at the possible involvement of the ‘chitta’ (synthetic drug) mafia and demanded an independent and thorough investigation into the incident. The two girls, who were close friends, had left their homes on November 14, reportedly telling their families they were going to Sundernagar in Mandi district to appear for an examination. Their bodies were recovered from Seer Khad near Barmana on November 15 and 16. Trilok Jamwal, the Bilaspur MLA, raised the issue during the ongoing Winter Session of the Himachal Pradesh Assembly. In response, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said a First Information Report (FIR) had been registered, and the police were investigating the case. He assured the House that a senior police officer would be assigned to supervise the investigation. The MLA’s concerns Jamwal sought the transfer of the investigation from Barmana police station to another police unit, alleging that the circumstances surrounding the girls’ deaths warranted an impartial probe. He also questioned where the two Class 10 students, aged 14 and 15, had stayed during the night between November 14 and 15. “The area where the incident took place is sensitive. The deaths of two minor girls is a serious matter. Could the ‘chitta’ mafia or any other mafia have any role in this tragedy? The government must investigate all possible angles,” Jamwal said. He also referred to an earlier incident in which a local women’s group at Laghat village near Bilaspur reportedly faced action for raising its voice against drug suppliers, and said the possibility of a drug mafia connection should not be overlooked. Leader of Opposition Jairam Thakur also termed the incident serious and demanded a comprehensive investigation, suggesting a Special Investigation Team be constituted to ensure a fair probe. Instagram, FB chats under scanner: CM CM Sukhu said the two girls, who had gone to Mandi with two youths on November 14, allegedly died by suicide. He also claimed that the girls had spoken to one of the youths using a labourer’s mobile phone. The police were also retrieving their Instagram and Facebook conversations to establish the circumstances leading to their deaths, he added.

content: Kullu: A car plunged more than 400 feet into a gorge in Lad Bharol area of Himachal Pradesh’s Mandi district late Tuesday night, killing six youths, including four minors.The accident occurred while the youths were returning home after attending a function in nearby Simas village, police said. headline: CM pushes for elimination of drug menace
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Wednesday directed deputy commissioners (DCs) and superintendents of police (SPs) of all districts to intensify coordinated efforts at the grassroots level to eliminate the menace of chitta (heroin) from the state.Chairing the 8th State-Level Narcotics Coordination (NCORD) meeting at Tapovan near Dharamshala in Kangra district, the CM emphasised that all officers must work collectively on the ground to achieve the goal of making the state completely chitta-free.He directed the authorities concerned to complete the mapping of peddlers and victims in all 246 panchayats identified under the red category before Dec 15, so that the campaign could be further accelerated.Seeking a report on the functioning of private de-addiction centres, Sukhu said that the state govt was committed to identifying chitta victims and providing them with the necessary support and rehabilitation.He added that govt would provide essential equipment to facilitate the identification of affected individuals and ensure their reintegration into the mainstream of society.The CM emphasised that the state govt would launch the ‘Khelo Himachal, Chitta Mukt Himachal’ campaign in December this year to strengthen public awareness and encourage collective participation in the fight against drug abuse.He said that govt had implemented the PIT-NDPS Act to ensure that habitual offenders involved in the supply of chitta were sent behind bars. Under the initiative, 159 people were put behind bars in 2026, the second highest in the country.He said that over the last three and a half years, the state govt has confiscated illegal properties worth about Rs 92 crore acquired by peddlers through drug trafficking.Sukhu said that strict action was also being taken against govt employees involved in drug trafficking. So far, 21 police personnel and 30 employees of other departments have been terminated from service. To expedite the trial of NDPS cases, the state govt had approved the establishment of two new NDPS courts.He further announced that govt would issue fresh Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for district-level NCORD meetings to ensure effective planning and coordinated action against chitta in every district.Directing officers to strengthen surveillance in identified red-category panchayats, the CM stressed that the campaign must be result-oriented, with accountability at every level. He also directed the deputy commissioner, Lahaul Spiti, to explore the feasibility of establishing a new prison spread over 200 bighas in Spiti for NDPS offenders and identify suitable land for the proposed facility.The CM reiterated that the state govt was determined to eradicate chitta and asked all departments and law enforcement agencies to work with a coordinated approach to protect the youth and secure the future of Himachal Pradesh.Chief Secretary K K Pant, additional chief secretary R D Nazeem, DGP Ashok Tiwari and other members of the committee were present at the meeting, while the DCs and SPs across the state joined virtually.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Proposal for new districts divides Himachal Congress, sparks dissent within Kangra leadership
content: The politically sensitive proposal to create new districts in Himachal Pradesh has stirred a hornet’s nest within the ruling Congress, exposing sharp differences among ministers and legislators and even triggering a heated exchange at the Congress Legislature Party (CLP) meeting in Dharamsala two days ago. With the issue gathering momentum, the disagreement has brought competing regional interests and political calculations to the forefront ahead of the 2027 Assembly poll.While Kangra, the state’s largest and politically most significant district, remains at the centre of the debate, the demand has now gained wider dimensions with Shimla and Mandi also emerging as possible candidates for administrative reorganisation.Public Works Minister Vikramaditya Singh on Wednesday made his opposition clear to any move to divide Shimla district and carve out a new district from it. He said the government had constituted a commission to examine the issue and the final picture would emerge only after its recommendations. However, he maintained that Shimla’s identity must remain intact.“My concern is Shimla district and I am very clear that its identity must remain intact and no new district should be created by dividing it,” he said. Vikramaditya added that he had discussed the matter with fellow legislators and people and there was opposition to breaking up the district.In Kangra, however, the Congress leadership remains divided. Ayurveda Minister Yadvinder Goma, Palampur MLA Ashish Butail and Fatehpur MLA Bhawani Pathania have supported the proposal, while Nagrota MLA Raghubir Bali and Jwalamukhi MLA Sanjay Rattan are opposed to dividing the district. Sources said the issue triggered heated exchanges among Kangra legislators during the CLP meeting in Dharamsala, with no consensus emerging.Bali has been among the most vocal opponents of the proposal, arguing that Kangra’s unity carries deep emotional significance for its people. While supporting the creation of hospitals and other facilities in every region, he said dividing the district into smaller administrative units would be the wrong approach.Pathania, however, said the proposal should be assessed purely on public interest rather than political considerations. “If people stand to benefit from the creation of a new district, why should it not be done? The move should not be driven by political gains but by people’s aspirations for better and swifter administration,” he said.He pointed out that certain areas were located nearly 200 km from their district headquarters, making administrative reorganisation a relevant consideration. Butail said granting district status to Palampur had been a long-standing demand of its residents. “We will place our viewpoint before the commission. Kangra has 15 Assembly segments and we too have emotional attachments, but we need to look at the issue in the present changed circumstances,” he said.The state government has constituted a commission headed by retired High Court judge Dharam Chand Chaudhary to examine the creation of new administrative units, including districts, subdivisions and blocks. The commission has been given six months to submit its report, well before the next Assembly elections scheduled for November 2027.Proposals being discussed include Dehra, Nurpur and Palampur in Kangra, Rampur in Shimla and Dharampur in Mandi. Previous Congress and BJP governments have also considered creating new districts but failed to take the proposals to their logical conclusion.A political dilemmaThe proposal to create new districts presents the Congress government with a delicate balancing act. While new administrative units could address long-standing regional demands and bring governance closer to people, the move also risks stirring competing territorial claims and emotional attachments to existing districtsWith Kangra, Shimla and Mandi all featuring in the debate, the government faces the challenge of reconciling regional aspirations with administrative priorities. As the 2027 Assembly elections approach, the decision could carry significant political implications, though whether it translates into electoral gains remains uncertain

headline: Jwala Nagar building collapse: Co-owner arrested while trying to flee; police probe conflicting claims over tenant’s 40-year stay
content: NEW DELHI A day after a building collapse in east Delhi’s Jwala Nagar claimed two lives, including that of a three-year-old boy, the Delhi Police on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) arrested one of the two co-owners of the property while he was allegedly attempting to flee. Delhi building collapse: Two killed, five injured as 50-year-old Jwala Nagar structure gives way storyline 1 The accused, identified as Veer Singh, was arrested in Shahdara, Deputy Commissioner of Police (Shahdara) R.P. Meena said. He is the brother of Surendar Singh, the other joint owner of the property, who was arrested on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), following the collapse, the officer said. According to the police, the property was originally registered in their mother’s name and was inherited by the two brothers after her death. Meanwhile, preliminary interrogation has yielded conflicting statements about how long the family of the three-year-old victim, Devansh, had been living in the building. The police said Surendar Singh allegedly told investigators that the family had been occupying the room for the past three years. However, the family maintains that they had been living in the same rented room for nearly four decades. The police said they were investigating the claims and verifying the ownership and tenancy details. The bodies of the two deceased, identified as Devansh alias Laddu (3) and Pintu (32), were handed over to their families for final rites after postmortem examinations. The five injured persons continue to receive treatment. The collapse occurred at around 10:09 a.m. on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), in Gali No. 6, near Peer Baba Mazar in the Sabji Mandi area of Jwala Nagar. The nearly 50-year-old building, which housed a gajak factory on the ground floor with residential rooms above it, gave way, trapping people under the debris. The injured were identified as Devansh’s mother, Khushbu (30); Vikesh (30); Akash (27); Dalip (26); and Aman (32). All seven victims were taken to Dr. Hedgewar Hospital, where Devansh and Pintu were declared dead. An FIR was registered under Sections 106(1) (causing death by negligence), 125(A) (causing hurt by a rash or negligent act endangering life or personal safety) and 223 (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Mr Meena had said Section 223 was added as the owner had allegedly failed to verify the tenants living in the property. The incident was the third building collapse in Delhi in November, following the collapse of an under-construction hotel in Paharganj, which injured eight workers, and a building collapse in Chawri Bazar on November 5, which claimed seven lives. Residents had alleged that they had repeatedly raised concerns about the deteriorating condition of the building, including a leaking roof, cracks in the walls and exposed metal girders, but the owner had failed to undertake necessary repairs. The MCD flagged the building’s proximity to the railway track (it stood approximately 24 metres away), and the vibrations caused by passing trains could have contributed to the collapse. Investigation into the case is underway.

headline: How 'depleted' India side defended SAFF title
content: CHENNAI: Whenever India head coach Naushad Moosa attended the press conference after every match in the SAFF Championship in Dhaka, words like 'depleted' and 'B team,' were thrown around often. While the number of outfield players came down from 25 to 17 in a blink, Moosa made it clear that his side was not a 'B' team. And they demonstrated just that, beating Pakistan 2-1 in the final on Tuesday to win a record-extending 10th title. While Moosa won the title as a player in 1997, his first as a coach hit different.  The circumstances Moosa was put into are key reasons why. Initially, the All India Football Federation (AIFF) announced a 28-member squad for the tournament, but three of them had returned to Mumbai City FC after game one over a reported agreement with the federation. Then, three more — Bijoy Varghese, Muhammad Suhail and Liston Colaco — had left to join the main senior team in New Zealand friendlies. Then, injuries piled up, leaving Moosa with just 17 outfield players and three goalkeepers. But Moosa and the players did not get discouraged. "From day one in Kolkata, I told them that it was going to be like this with the squad. I made them understand there might be possibilities of a depleted squad. They were well aware and they knew what to do," he told this daily on Thursday. But facing a full-strength Pakistan side — with diaspora players plying their trade in Europe — was not going to be easy. With India trailing at half-time, Moosa revealed what he said to lift the side in the dressing room during the break. "So the first thing I told the players was that we are being too nice. They were doing everything possible to irritate us, they were doing everything to kill us. So we cannot let that happen. Then the players themselves got spurred and it reflected in the second half," he said. India then tilted the momentum in their favour, as Suhail levelled in the 60th minute. But Sandip Mandi's header in the 88th minute won them the title. .For Fernandes' side, Iran win in qualifier a blueprint ahead of tough U17 Asian Cup .The players he had did not have the requisite match fitness. One crucial factor Moosa believed that got the team through is the transparency between the players and coaching staff. "The likes of Suhail Bhat (who ended as the top scorer with four goals) have not played 90 minutes of football. In the first match, he did not hide his intention to be subbed off but as the tournament progressed, he was able to drag on till the final whistle. That shows how much they wanted the team to win. It was never about themselves. My assistant coach Bibiano (Fernandes) played a very important role, my analyst Joy Gabriel and even the goalkeeping coach (Parshuram Salwadi) were taking responsibilities to help me. Everybody out there wanted to win this badly," he said.India began their tournament by beating a rotated Pakistan team 3-2. Then, they posted a narrow 1-0 victory against Maldives before beating Bhutan 2-1 in the semifinals. Familiarity with the players due to their time in the U23 team, coached by Moosa, helped him. "We did not have the time to prepare. Firstly, I was left with players from three teams: Mumbai City, Punjab FC and Kerala Blasters. But it was good of Mohun Bagan who sent three players: Suhail, Priyansh Dubey, and Abhishek (Suryavanshi). So I got these three players. But the others like Brison Fernandes,  Mandi and Vishnu PV knew the kind of football we are looking for, which really helped," Moosa said.  .Racism row: AIFF set to file complaint, U17 Palestinian player apologises.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Keralam CM’s claims incorrect, judicial probe needed into power purchase deals, says Pinarayi Vijayan
content: THIRUVANANTHAPURAM While Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan has chosen to dismiss allegations related to the power purchase deal with VEH Global India Ltd as baseless, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on Thursday said the Chief Minister’s explanation has only served to deepen the mystery. At a press conference here, Mr. Vijayan reiterated his demand for a judicial probe into contentious power purchase deals and asked the government to make public all documents related to the GNA Energy-Himachal Pradesh government power supply offers and the power purchase agreement with VEH Global India Pvt Ltd. The Chief Minister’s justification that electricity was procured from VEH Global via a bilateral arrangement as there were no takers for tenders floated by the Kerala State Electricity Board (KSEB) was incorrect, Mr. Vijayan said. While the tender for peak-hour supply was opened only on September 29, the agreement with VEH Global had already been signed on September 23, he said. Further, 19 companies had quoted per-unit prices below ₹10 in a September 10 tender, he said. Moreover, the contract with VEH Global for supply at ₹11 per unit in October was unnecessary as the State did not face any power shortage that month, he said. Keralam had in hand 788 MW through three earlier contracts and another 300 MW via a ‘swap’ arrangement. Also, the agreement was signed for ₹11 per unit when wind energy costs do not exceed ₹4, he added. Corruption charges According to Mr. Vijayan, corruption worth ₹252 crore was intended through the deal, but it fell through only because wind energy was in short supply and the firm was unable to supply the contracted 200 MW on most days. “But the depth and seriousness of the intended corruption does not disappear because of that,” he said.

headline: Amritpal Singh’s Punjab homecoming: Family expects big turnout, but his village is divided
content: A poster reading “Jee aayan nu" (welcome), with Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh gazing out, greets you as you step into his village of Jallupur Khera in Amritsar district. Big “Parking” signs then lead you to his house near Gurdwara Kala Mehar, which once became his centre of sorts. It is 10 am and his father Tarsem Singh, now called “Bapu ji”, sits cross-legged, surrounded by some guests. “A lot of people had gathered here last Saturday because news had spread about his release, but they went back disappointed,” says Tarsem, dressed in a gleaming white kurta-pyjama. Amritpal, 33, the Independent MP of Khadoor Sahib constituency and the face of Akali Dal (Waris Punjab De), has been lodged in Assam's Dibrugarh Central Jail since his arrest on April 23, 2023. This was preceded by a month-long manhunt that ensued when he and his supporters stormed the Ajnala police station in the district on February 23 to free an aide. After his NSA detention expired in April 2026, the Punjab Police re-arrested him in the Ajnala case, and he continues to be held in Dibrugarh. He has been given a three-hour parole on November 21 to attend the cremation of his grandmother, Charan Kaur, 84, who died on November 8. It will be the first time he is returning to Punjab since his arrest. Tarsem, who says the family speaks to Amritpal — the sole prisoner in the Ajnala case lodged in Dibrugarh — once or twice a week, expects a large crowd on the day. Some, such as Arsh Umriana from Moga, are already here. The unsmiling man tells you to check social media for more about him. “I toured the entire state on a bicycle to campaign for AAP.” He has now switched to Waris Punjab De and was their poll in charge in Faridkot during the 2024 parliamentary polls. As the conversation veers towards the coming Assembly elections, Tarsem says they have already declared candidates for 48 seats. Remind him that the party has yet to get registration from the Election Commission and he calls it yet another example of “dhakka” (injustice). "They are ignoring the will of the people. We have two elected MPs, my son won his seat by the highest margin of 1.97 lakh votes in Punjab.” Tarsem insists the party has a real chance because Punjab needs a regional force. "The present one (Akali Dal) is hand in glove with the Centre. Look how they (BJP) have delayed the SGPC polls to favour the Akalis.” The SGPC, or the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, is the apex religious organisation responsible for the management, maintenance, and administration of gurdwaras in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, and Chandigarh. Tarsem dismisses fears about law and order and Amritpal's “anti-national” rhetoric. "He has taken an oath on the Constitution. We are committed to staying within its confines,” he declares. The party's agenda, he says, is "to safeguard the youth of the state and its interests. We believe in ‘sarbat da bhalla’ (the welfare of all). We treat all religions as equal." The release of Bandi Singhs (prisoners held during militancy) is also an issue. "How can you continue to detain people who have already served their sentence?" The story of a Bandi Singh Not too far away is the house of Gurdeep Singh Khera, 65, who has been in jail since his arrest in Delhi in 1990 in a bomb blast case. He has been acquitted in one case and has just returned to Amritsar jail this week after a month-long parole. A big black-and-white picture of a boy dominates the living room. "It is of his younger brother Kulwinder Singh, 20, who was picked up by the police in 1992 and never found again,” says his wife Gurjit Kaur, whom he married when he was out on parole in March 2017. She says she visited Amritpal's house after the death of his grandmother but does not plan to meet him. "My husband is a Bandi Singh, but Amritpal has never visited our home even though we live down the lane. Only the Akalis have supported us.” Gurjit says they were impressed when Amritpal started his drive to baptise youngsters to keep them away from drugs. "But my husband was very upset when he stormed the Ajnala police station with Sri Guru Granth Sahib … look at the number of youngsters who were arrested all because of him.” At the other end of the village, sarpanch Gurpreet Kaur from Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) simply shrugs when you ask her about the parole. “Not all youngsters in the village are with him; most of his supporters come from outside,” she says, hazarding a guess. Her 27-year-old son Gaganpreet Singh, a slightly built youngster with a twirling moustache, says they have never had much to do with him. Amritpal's family, he says, declared a candidate of their choice as the unanimously elected sarpanch two weeks before the 2024 elections. "I was a strong candidate, but since the seat was reserved for women, my mother contested. The villagers did not support the family and went ahead with the elections. We won by over 200 votes.” ‘Ralwan-milwan’ Such voices are not confined to Jallupur Khera. Jobanjit Singh, a JCB driver from Tarn Taran that forms part of the Khadoor Sahib constituency, says the response to the parole is “ralwan-milwan” (mixed). “In 2024, there was a wave in his favour, but people are more cautious now,” he says. In the small market at Pheruman, an athletic Baljit Singh, the owner of Sandhu Dairy with an arm covered with tattoos, says Amritpal draws his popularity from a simple Punjabi trait. "We don't like ‘dhakka’ or ‘zyadti’ (excess). Amritpal was just another NRI, but the government came down heavily on him, and that's how we started supporting him." Kulbir Singh from Saron says he remains popular among a section of youngsters because of his continued incarceration. “The Ajnala incident was not good, but that does not mean you will keep him inside forever?" But Mahinder Pal Singh, the area manager of a cattle feed company, cautions against “garam khyali” (extremist thinking). “It never ends well.” Then there is this group of young fans, among them Armandeep Singh, a Class 10 student from Gurdaspur. "We will vote for Amritpal," he says, lifting his chin. Tell him he is underage and he shrugs: “I will get my family to vote for him.” Near the 17th-Century Bhora Sahib gurdwara at Baba Bakala, shopkeepers are more disapproving. “Youngsters are drawn in by his bravado," says Harjinder Singh. "But you have to be pragmatic. He has been telling youths to carry a three-to-four-foot siri sahib (sword). Come night and some of these very young men do ‘loot khasoot’ under the influence of intoxicants." Back home, Tarsem dismisses such claims as a “smear campaign”. “They are scared of the love people have for him. He will sweep the polls.” Gagandeep, the proxy sarpanch, shrugs. “It is not that simple ji. Everything is not black and white.” (Manraj Grewal Sharma is National Editor, North, The Indian Express)

headline: 11 states, Union Territories are ‘fully literate’; Madhya Pradesh leads in adult learners
content: As many as 11 states and Union Territories (UTs) have declared themselves “fully literate” under the Centre’s adult literacy initiative ULLAS–Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram. These are Ladakh, Mizoram, Goa, Tripura, Himachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, and Lakshadweep. Officials said “achieving 95% literacy in a state or UT is… equivalent to being fully literate, as 100% literacy is not possible due to reasons such as advanced age of some people and certain intellectual disabilities that may affect ability to read and write.” Over 90.96 lakh learners aged 15 and above have taken the Foundational Literacy and Numeracy Assessment Test (FLNAT) this academic year. “. FLNAT is a mechanism under ULLAS to evaluate learners’ reading, writing and numeracy skills. Successful learners are certified as ‘Literate’ by the National Institute of Open Schooling,” said a government official. The FLNAT is conducted twice a year, according to Ministry of Education data. More than 90.96 lakh learners have appeared in 2026-27 so far. Overall, 4.15 crore learners across 34 states and UTs have taken the test, with a success rate above 90%. Madhya Pradesh leads with 20.43 lakh adult learners, followed by Rajasthan (18.18 lakh), Odisha (12 lakh), Telangana (7.54 lakh), Maharashtra (6.5 lakh) and Tamil Nadu (4.5 lakh). The Department of School Education and Literacy has been implementing the ULLAS–Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram since 2022-23, said officials. Also Read | International Literacy Day 2026: Why is it celebrated, history, theme and significance “In pursuance of NEP 2020, the scheme targets non-literate persons aged 15 and above. The scheme is being implemented in a hybrid mode through volunteerism, utilising school and higher education institution (HEI) platforms and community engagement. It consists of five components — foundational literacy and numeracy, critical life skills, basic education, vocational skills and continuing education,” the official said. Officials said the scheme has raised India’s literacy rate to 81.1%, from 74.04% in Census 2011. More than 4.17 crore learners and 52.89 lakh volunteer teachers have registered on the ULLAS mobile app.

The yield of blue-chip companies is higher compared to other companies. How many of the statements given above are correct? (a) Only one (b) Only two (c) All three (d) None Relevance: The question is relevant to concepts such as equity investment, market capitalisation, dividend yield and investment risk. It links financial markets with corporate performance, investor behaviour and capital formation. Explanation — Blue-chip stocks, also known as large-caps, have led the market’s rally over the past three weeks, after underperforming for nearly a year. As geopolitical concerns have eased, and other valuation and growth-related concerns have subsided for now, this premium section of the market has emerged as the most attractive risk-reward bet for investors. According to www.investopedia.com, — "A blue chip is a stable and well-established company known for its reliable financial performance. Blue chip stocks are often part of major market indexes and are popular among conservative investors. Hence, statement 1 is correct. — Blue chips are considered safer investments but typically yield lower returns compared to high-growth companies. Hence, statement 3 is not correct. — Blue-chip companies are not completely risk-free. Their share prices can decline due to market volatility, economic downturns, poor business decisions or other financial challenges." Hence, statement 2 is not correct. Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer. QUESTION 4 Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax in India applies to which of the following? 1. Equity Mutual Funds 2. Real Estate (Immovable Property) 3. Capital Assets Select the correct answer using the codes given below: (a) 2 only (b) 1 and 2 only (c) 3 only (d) 1, 2 and 3 Relevance: The question is relevant to the taxation of financial instruments, equity mutual funds and immovable property. It tests understanding of capital gains taxation and the distinction between short-term and long-term capital gains. Explanation — The third pre-budget consultation with experts and leaders from manufacturing also saw industry bodies suggesting rationalisation of Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax on listed securities. Citing concerns over substantial foreign investment outflows earlier this year, the Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI) stressed on the need to reduce LTCG tax or allow foreign investors to compute capital gains in the currency of their original investment. — LTCG tax applies to gains from the sale of equity-oriented mutual fund units held for more than 12 months. Under Section 112A, gains exceeding the applicable annual exemption limit are taxed at 12.5%. Hence, 1 is correct. — LTCG tax applies to gains from the sale of immovable property held for more than 24 months. The applicable tax treatment depends on the date of acquisition and the relevant provisions of the Income-tax Act. Hence, 2 is correct. — Long-term capital gains arise from the transfer of capital assets held beyond the prescribed holding period. The holding period varies according to the nature of the asset. Hence, 3 is correct. Therefore, option (d) is the correct answer. (Other Source: www.incometaxindia.gov.in) QUESTION 5 With reference to headline inflation, consider the following statements: 1. It is measured through the Wholesale Price Index (WPI). 2. Goods and services are both included in the calculation of headline inflation. Which of the statements given above is/are correct? (a) 1 only (b) 2 only (b) Both 1 and 2 (d) Neither 1 nor 2 Relevance: The question tests understanding of inflation measurement and the distinction between headline and core inflation. It links inflation measurement with monetary policy, RBI's inflation-targeting framework and macroeconomic stability. Explanation — Headline inflation was less than 4% in only five out of 36 states and union territories (Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, and NCT of Delhi). Meanwhile, it was higher than 6% in 11 states and union territories. It was the highest in Puducherry (7.96%). — In India, headline inflation is measured through the WPI (the latest base year 2011-12) – which consists of 697 commodities (services are not included in WPI in India). It is measured on year-on-year basis i.e., rate of change in price level in a given month vis a vis corresponding month of last year. This is also known as point to point inflation. Hence, statement 1 is correct and statement 2 is not correct. — In India, there are three main components in WPI – Primary Articles (weight: 22.62%), Fuel & Power (weight: 13.15%) and Manufactured Products (weight: 64.23). Within WPI, Food Inflation is also calculated on year-on-year basis. Therefore, option (a) is the correct answer. headline: Corruption charges rock Himachal assembly on third day of winter session
content: Dharamshala: The Himachal Pradesh Assembly witnessed heated exchanges over corruption on Wednesday, the third day of its winter session, as BJP and Congress members traded allegations during a discussion on an adjournment motion.The BJP targeted the govt over alleged corruption in the Pekhubela solar power project in Una, irregularities in Hamirpur bus stand construction and industrial scrap disposal, besides accusing it of shielding a transfer mafia.Opening the discussion under Rule 67, BJP MLA Vinod Kumar alleged that rates had been fixed for transferring TGTs, JBTs and principals, with ruling party politicians extorting money from teachers. He termed it a multi-crore scam and alleged that a scrap mafia was operating in Baddi, Solan.Chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu challenged the opposition to produce evidence, promising probes into substantiated allegations and jail for those found guilty. He also warned Kumar of action if his allegation that bills for constituency works were being withheld in the Treasury proved false.Kumar also questioned the cost of the 32 MW Pekhubela solar power project in Una, built at a cost of Rs 220 crore, claiming that a 35 MW project in Gujarat had been installed for Rs 140 crore. Alleging that the cost of the Hamirpur bus stand had escalated to over Rs 200 crore against sanctioned amount of Rs 42 crore, he demanded action against those responsible.Leader of opposition Jai Ram Thakur alleged that the govt was trying to suppress the opposition‘s voice and asked whether it had the right to question govt.The discussion also saw a confrontation over the state’s debt. Sukhu cited a debt figure of Rs 76,830 crore left by the previous BJP govt, while the LoP disputed govt’s figures, claiming that the debt had crossed Rs 1 lakh crore during the present govt’s tenure.Industries minister Rajesh Dharmani accused the previous BJP govt of giving land to outsider-owned industries in Baddi at throwaway prices.
