headline: Fake epilepsy, diabetes drugs made using chalk, lactose at illegal Himachal factory; 2 held
content: MEERUT/SHIMLA: An illegal pharmaceutical factory allegedly manufacturing counterfeit medicines used to treat epilepsy, diabetes, typhoid and other ailments using substances such as chalk and lactose was busted in Himachal Pradesh's Solan district on Thursday following a joint operation by Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) and drug authorities. Two men were arrested from the unit, which operated without a manufacturing licence from a residential building in Rajpura village near Nalagarh. Investigators recovered nearly 67,000 antibiotic tablets, 6,500 Pregabalin capsules, raw materials and machinery used to manufacture and package the drugs.The raid followed an investigation into counterfeit medicines seized from a medical shop in Kuraina village of Varanasi on Oct 30. Pharmaceutical companies whose brand names appeared on the seized medicines identified them as spurious, prompting police to register an FIR. On Wednesday, UP STF and Varanasi police arrested Abhishek Singh for allegedly distributing counterfeit medicines in Bihar and Jharkhand. During questioning, he disclosed that the drugs were being sourced from the Solan factory, leading investigators to the unit.The factory allegedly manufactured Pregabalin capsules (used to treat epilepsy, seizures and neuropathic pain); C-Z tablets containing Cefixime and Azithromycin (prescribed for bacterial infections, including typhoid and urinary tract infections); PAN D (used to treat acid reflux and ulcers); and Metformin Hydrochloride (prescribed for type 2 diabetes). Investigators also recovered raw drug pellets and packaging materials. Pregabalin falls under Schedule H1 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945, while the other prescription medicines are regulated under Schedule H. These medicines require prescriptions from registered medical practitioners.Additional SP Brijesh Kumar Singh of UP STF's Meerut field unit said the accused were using chalk and lactose as raw materials to manufacture counterfeit medicines. "We've arrested two men from the factory. Raw materials used to make these drugs were chalk and lactose," Singh said.The arrested men, Monu Mehta from Jharkhand and Mohammad Haseen from Saharanpur, operated the manufacturing machinery and handled dispatches. Singh said they were recruited by Sunil Kumar, a Badaun resident who allegedly owned the factory and had previously been arrested and jailed in a counterfeit medicine case in Varanasi. Sunil remained absconding. The two men received monthly salaries of Rs 15,000 to Rs 20,000. Haseen had joined the unit seven months earlier, while Mehta had worked there for about a year.A joint team of Meerut UP STF, UP Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) and Himachal Pradesh State Drugs Control Administration raided the premises. Himachal Pradesh state drug controller Manish Kapoor told TOI that his department received information from UP STF and FSDA on Wednesday evening and immediately formed a team of five drug inspectors. "We constituted a team of five drug inspectors, carried out search and seizure operation entire night and arrested two persons with nearly 67,000 antibiotic tablets and 6,500 Pregabalin capsules," Kapoor said.The search also yielded two capsule-filling machines, blister-packing machines, an air compressor, unfinished pharmaceutical materials and packaging equipment. Investigators found that the unit lacked a manufacturing licence and that the seized medicines carried labels falsely claiming they were manufactured in Sirmaur district of Himachal Pradesh. Kapoor said the products were suspected to be substandard and authorities were examining the manufacturing and distribution network.Dr Harish Mohan Rastogi, a physician, warned that counterfeit medicines could put patients at serious risk, particularly those undergoing treatment for epilepsy, diabetes and infections. "Some of these are lifesaving drugs like Pregabalin and Metformin Hydrochloride meant to treat kidney infections, epilepsy and diabetes. The counterfeit one will not affect the patients, leading to emergencies and can be life-threatening. Similarly, others are antibiotics for different infections like typhoid and allergies," he told TOI.The FIR registered in Varanasi invoked BNS sections 61(2) (criminal conspiracy), 111 (organised crime), 318(4) (cheating involving delivery of property), 336(3) (forgery with intent to cheat), 276 (adulteration of drugs) and 278 (selling a drug as a different drug). A Nalagarh court remanded Mehta and Haseen to the custody of Himachal Pradesh State Drugs Control Administration until Nov 23. UP STF was also searching for Sunil and tracing the distribution of suspected counterfeit medicines in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Jharkhand.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Meerut | Silver Rate in Meerut | Bank Holidays in Meerut | Public Holidays in Meerut | Meerut AQI | Weather in Meerut | Petrol Price in Meerut | Diesel Price in Meerut | CNG Price in Meerut | LPG Price in MeerutStay updated with the latest Meerut news. headline: BJP will oppose govt. move to scrap anti-conversion and anti-cow slaughter laws: Ashok
content: MANGALURU The Bharatiya Janata Party will strongly oppose any move by the State government to bring amendments and allow religious conversion and cow slaughter, said Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly R. Ashok in Mangaluru on Thursday. Talking to reporters, Mr. Ashok said Congress MLC Ivan D’souza recently spoke about the government intending to bring amendment to allow religious conversion. “This is nothing but the continued act of the Congress to appease a section of minorities. The BJP will strongly oppose amendments to allow religious conversion.” Mr. Ashok said the BJP will also oppose any move that allows cow slaughter. He said the State Cabinet is set to clear a proposal to transfer ₹50,000 to accounts of each minority student for purchase of laptop. The government has granted ₹100 crore for development of Urdu schools. The Minority Welfare Department has communalised recruitment to defence forces by calling applications of minority community members for six months training. There was marked increase in grants to minority welfare schemes, while grants to SCs, STs, Bhovi Nigams, and other community welfare corporations have been cut down, he said. Mr. Ashok said by implementing guarantee schemes, the Congress government has pushed the State towards bankruptcy. Kerala and Himachal Pradesh were already under bankruptcy. He said in the forthcoming Budget the State government has to take a loan of over ₹1.5 lakh crore to run the guarantee schemes.

headline: Rich country, poor sanitation: SC's message on waste crisis
content: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has observed that Bharat has become a rich country but continues to perform poorly on sanitation, warning that shortcomings in waste management are undermining the country’s progress in other fields.A Bench of Justices SVN Bhatti and NV Anjaria made the observation on November 17 while hearing appeals arising from National Green Tribunal (NGT) orders concerning municipal corporations’ compliance with environmental norms under the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026.“The court notes that Bharat is now a rich country but has poor sanitation performance. The growth achieved in other fields is completely negated by the negative impact from this manageable dereliction by all the stakeholders,” the Bench said in its order.The case stems from NGT orders pulling up municipal corporations for violations of environmental norms under the SWM Rules. The Supreme Court is now supervising their implementation across the country.The Bench acknowledged that the first two phases of the process, initiating implementation and putting in place an administrative mechanism to monitor compliance with the SWM Rules, had been completed.However, it flagged the gap between administrative progress and actual sanitation outcomes, observing that shortcomings in waste management were negating the gains achieved in other sectors.The court described the lapses as a “manageable dereliction” involving all stakeholders, including the Centre, state governments, civic bodies and citizens, indicating that the sanitation crisis was not insurmountable but required effective implementation and accountability.The observations are likely to put municipal corporations under greater pressure to demonstrate compliance on the ground, including proper waste segregation, cleaner streets and scientific waste processing, rather than relying solely on plans, committees and affidavits.The next hearing will examine whether the monitoring mechanism translates into tangible improvements in waste management and sanitation across the country..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: BJP Seeks Apology From Himachal Pradesh Minister Jagat Singh Negi Over Operation Sindoor Remarks

headline: New rural employment scheme Viksit Bharat Rozgar Mission would have cost states six times than MGNREGA in 2025-26: Report
content: New Delhi: States would have spent around Rs 33,000 crore – six times more than what it actually spent – in 2025-26 if Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) was in place instead of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGA), a new report has said. .The VB-G RAM G had replaced MGNREGA on July 1 this year. .According to State of State Finances 2026-27 prepared by PRS Legislative Research, states have to pay a larger share under VB-G RAM G, the tweaked rural employment guarantee scheme. .Months without pay leaves rural employment scheme staff in distress.“Had VB-G RAM G been in place instead of MGNREGA in 2025-26, states would have spent around Rs 33,000 crore, assuming the same number of person days and wage rates. This is around six times what they actually spent under MGNREGA (Rs 5,261 crore),” it said. .For Karnataka, its share was Rs 151 crore in 2025-26 when MGNREGA was in place but it would have risen to Rs 1,380 crore if VB-G RAM G was in place. .Large states like Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh would have seen an additional state spending of Rs 2,000-3,000 crore in 2025-26 if VB-G RAM G was in place. .With the draft VB-G RAM G Rules proposing that a state’s share in the central allocation will be based on the devolution parameters of the 16th Finance Commission, six states would have fallen short of the central fund requirement in 2025-26. .These states -- Andhra Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura -- could have borne an excess expenditure ranging Rs 80 crore to Rs 650 crore. .Viksit Bharat Rozgar Mission to rollout from July 1, guarantees 125 days of rural employment.With the union government notifying a minimum wage rate of Rs 300 per day in July under the new scheme, the report said, the VB-G RAM G would have cost states around seven times their actual 2025-26 spending under MGNREGA. .It highlighted that till the rules are notified, the union government has decided to allocate state-wise funding for 2026-27 based on the funds released under MGNREGA in 2024-25.

headline: Chitkul: A Picturesque Himalayan Village In Himachal Pradesh
content: Nestled in Himachal Pradesh’s Baspa Valley, Chitkul is often described as the last inhabited village on the old Indo-Tibet route. Located at around 3,450 metres, it is known for its traditional wooden houses, scenic Himalayan views and the Baspa River.

headline: Ambuja Neotia to invest about ₹2,700 crore in hotels, almost triple room capacity
content: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. The Ambuja Neotia Group plans to invest ₹2,700 crore in its hospitality business over four to five years, almost tripling its hotel room capacity as it expands into new destinations. Parthiv Neotia, the company’s managing director and head of healthcare, said in an exclusive interview with Mint that the Kolkata-based group currently has 12 hotels with about 900 rooms across five states. It has 1,100 rooms under construction across nine projects. The expansion is focused on West Bengal and later, it will look at projects in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Assam and Chhattisgarh. “We are primarily focused on the five-star and five-star deluxe categories. But we also understand that every hotel cannot be a five-star property and will need to create supply in markets where there is an opportunity for a different category of hotel,” Neotia said. In the next five years, there will be about 2,550 rooms across 28 hotels in eight states, he added. The group's hotels are managed by the Tata Group’s Indian Hotels Co Ltd (IHCL) and primarily has the Taj brand in its portfolio as well as one SeleQtions property. Guwahati is one city where it is considering a mid-market hotel as well. Neotia said the company has invested ₹2,500 crore in its hotel projects till date. The group is developing more affordable hotels in locations such as Digha, West Bengal, while other projects are planned in Lataguri, the Sunderbans and Shimla.

headline: Indore Forests Record 449 Livestock Kills By Leopards In 7 Years, Yet No Budget To Prevent Attacks
content: Indore (Madhya Pradesh): Leopards killed livestock 449 times in Indore Forest Division over seven years, and 172 conflict hotspots have been identified. Yet the division has no provision for preventive measures and no separate budget for them; only compensation is paid after the loss.A geographical analysis by IFS officer Pradeep Mishra of 2019-25 records found Mhow recorded the most incidents (147), followed by Choral (110), Manpur (102) and Indore (90). Mhow, Choral and Manpur together accounted for 359, nearly 80% of the total.No provision, no fundsMishra said territorial divisions like Indore have no provision for preventing leopard kills and no separate budget. He plans to take the study to headquarters to develop a prevention strategy. “Possibly, we can divert leopard movement away from residents,” he said. Asked whether such kills can be prevented, he said measures can be taken, and they help. Trials elsewhere support this. Annual compensation more than doubled, from Rs 4.92 lakh in 2019 to Rs 11.24 lakh in 2025. This covers cattle kills only, not all 449 livestock losses.Standard precautionsStandard advisories include sheltering cattle in roofed, wire-sealed sheds before dusk; overnight lights or radios; clearing cover within 100 metres of pens; avoiding dawn and dusk grazing near forest edges; guard dogs; clearing garbage to keep strays away; and reporting pugmarks to the Forest Department.Villagers rely on fencing, lighting, group grazingThere is palpable fear among villagers affected leopards attacking their livestock. Mangilal Patel, 63, Jalyamau village said “We have put fencing around our house. We come inside early in the evening and avoid going into the forest alone.” Similarly, Babulal, 42, of Chalya village said, “Two of us go together when taking the cattle to graze in the forest so the leopard does not attack.” Shyamlal Gehlot, 50, of Malendi village said, “We keep a light bulb on at night and also keep pet dogs. We take our cattle out to graze together in groups.” Nisha Banarji, 38, also of Malendi said, “We have put thorny fencing around our house and tie our cattle inside the shed at home.”Three conflict clusters“Using KDE and Getis-Ord Gi* hotspot analysis, I identified 172 statistically significant hotspot cells among 1,352 examined, covering about 22% of the forest extent. The incidents are concentrated in three clusters: a central belt, a southwestern cluster and a northeastern chain around Choral Range.”— Pradeep Mishra, IFS officerWhat has worked elsewherePauri Garhwal: Wildlife Institute of India trials of flashing solar lights around 27 villages cut nocturnal livestock kills by nearly 50%.Himachal Pradesh: Studded collars on free-grazing cattle showed a 100% drop in fatal throat bites in field trials.Himachal and Ladakh: Reinforced, roofed stone-and-wire pens sharply cut “surplus killing” in sheds.Kanha Tiger Reserve: Conflict data guides targeted patrols and grazing advisories.Level up your brain the fun way. headline: Always a Soldier: Vijai Singh Mankotia’s legacy in uniform and Himachal politics
content: Vijai Singh Mankotia was at his dining table, preparing notes in his diary for an upcoming meeting of the Himachal Pradesh chapter of the Indian Ex-Services League (IESL) on Tuesday morning, when he collapsed. At Dharamshala’s Sainik Bhawan, ex-servicemen who had gathered for the Tuesday meeting were waiting for Mankotia’s arrival when their phones lit up with the news that he had been taken to the Kangra hospital. It was only later that they found out from Mankotia’s driver, Varun, that even in his final hours, the retired Major’s thoughts were with them. On September 29, 2026, Mankotia suffered a heart attack at his ancestral home in Tiara village in Himachal’s Kangra district and died at the Kangra hospital during treatment, aged 87. By the time he retired from the Army in 1976, he had served in the India-China War of 1962 and the India-Pakistan wars of 1965 and 1971. He then forayed into Himachal politics, which remained his arena for the next four decades. He was a five-time MLA from Himachal’s Shahpur and served as a state cabinet minister twice. “I called him on Monday morning, and we discussed the IESL meeting schedule at length. In the end, he said in our local dialect, ‘Mangle rakhi lo… mangle (Keep this meeting for Tuesday)’, and the meeting was called for the next day,” Col YS Rana (Rtd), the IESL Himachal chapter president who rushed from Sainik Bhawan to Mankotia’s bedside at the hospital on September 29, tells The Indian Express, adding, “He was a lifelong member of our league.” Friends and colleagues remember Mankotia for taking a stand when it mattered and prioritising personal relationships over professional or political differences that developed throughout his life. For roughly 40 years until 2023, Mankotia served as the president of the IESL’s Himachal chapter. “He was an honest, straightforward man, someone who stood firmly by his convictions,” says Brigadier Khushal Singh Thakur (YSM), a Kargil War veteran. Nationally, the IESL was among the ex-servicemen's organisations involved in discussions around One Rank, One Pension (OROP), which the government approved in 2015. In Himachal Pradesh, the league had long demanded the removal of population-based criteria in Army recruitment and an increase in the state's share of recruitment, but these demands remain unresolved. The IESL Himachal chapter has now urged Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu to name Government Degree College, Shahpur, after Mankotia. Politics and bonds After Mankotia entered politics, Himachal’s Shahpur assembly constituency gave him his first electoral win in 1982, as an Independent candidate. He joined the Congress in 1985 and retained the seat. He crossed over to V P Singh’s Jan Morcha in 1989 and won Shahpur on a Janata Dal ticket in 1990. He later returned to the Congress fold in 1993 and won the seat a fourth time. Contemporaries say Sanjay Gandhi, who died in 1980, influenced his decision to become a politician. “Mankotia sometimes joked that Sanjay Gandhi died the day after he joined politics. He was very close to him. Many believed his political journey might have taken a different course had Sanjay Gandhi lived,” Colonel Rana says. For the next four decades, Mankotia was difficult to ignore in Himachal politics. In 1995, he became the Tourism and Civil Aviation Minister in the Virbhadra Singh-led Congress government. He served until 1998. Though he lost the 1998 Shahpur Assembly election, he returned in 2003, winning the seat a fifth time on a Congress ticket. He also returned to the Cabinet for a short stint from March 2003 to July 2004. Vijai Singh Mankotia and Virbhadra Singh, who knew each other from their school days at Bishop Cotton School, however, had their share of disagreements. “Not everyone remembers that Virbhadra Singh played a role in bringing Mankotia back into the Congress fold after his first electoral victory as an Independent. But their relationship was complicated: they could work together, but their differences often resurfaced,” a senior Congress leader recalls, on the condition of anonymity. One of the most contentious episodes of Mankotia’s political career came in 2007, when he levelled corruption allegations against Virbhadra Singh and released an audio CD purportedly supporting his claims. However, Virbhadra Singh and his wife, Pratibha Singh, were later acquitted in the case registered against them over that audio CD. In 2007, Mankotia joined the BSP and contested the Dharamshala Assembly, which he lost. He later returned to the Congress in 2012, contested from Shahpur again but lost as well. In 2017, he contested Shahpur as an Independent but lost again. He joined the BJP in October 2022. As a politician, what worked for Mankotia was the personal bonds he developed with voters. Abhimanyu Verma, a Shahpur resident whose family had seen the retired Major from his early days in politics, says, “He was like a member of our family. Since 2004, we have organised a jagran at our house every year on May 8. I cannot recall an occasion when he missed it. He came from Delhi, Rajasthan or Mumbai, postponing or cancelling other engagements.” Sarveen Chaudhary, the BJP leader who defeated Mankotia in the last 2017 Assembly election, remembers him as a politician who never lost touch with the people in Shahpur. “His popularity can be gauged from how the people of Shahpur elected him five times. He was down-to-earth, showed no discrimination,” she says, adding, “We had political differences, but he never allowed those differences to affect our personal relationship.” Perhaps it's because of this nature that Mankotia’s death prompted condolence messages from across the political spectrum — from Chief Minister Sukhu to Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur and Union Minister JP Nadda. Love for cricket Mankotia studied at Bishop Cotton School in Shimla and pursued higher education in Punjab before he joined the Indian Military Academy (IMA) in Dehradun in 1960. At the IMA, “he was awarded the coveted Sword of Honour, the Gold Medal, the Infantry Prize, the English Prize and the Declamation Contest Prize,” says Colonel Sangram Mankotia (retd), his first cousin. After graduating from the IMA, he joined the Army in June 1962 with the Gorkha Rifles and rose through the ranks to become Major. He eventually retired in 1976. His family, Sangram says, traces its ancestry to Mankote in the Poonch region of Jammu and Kashmir, from where they eventually moved to Himachal’s Kangra valley. Mankotia grew up with five siblings, and among them, his cousin remembers him as the most charming, a man with a passion for cricket and a penchant for discussing the sport like a professional. “He even received a Cricket Blue in recognition of his achievements as a cricketer (at IMA),” the cousin adds. Mankotia leaves behind his wife, Jaishree, who belongs to the erstwhile royal family of Kota Kunadi in Rajasthan, and their two children. Son Yudhveer Singh Mankotia, 58, is settled in Abu Dhabi, and daughter Samyukta Singh, 57, lives in Gujarat. Talking about his father, Yudhveer says, “From discussions about cricket to political upheavals in the state and the country, there are countless memories, which cannot be summed up in a few words.”

headline: DA hike: Jharkhand, Mizoram, Odisha govts increase dearness allowance — Check how much, who is eligible, details
content: DA hike news: The state governments of Jharkhand, Mizoram and Odisha have each announced increase in dearness allowance and dearness relief, according to a separate PTI reports this week.Notably, after the Finance Ministry's announcement on 28 October, a number of state governments also hiked DA for employees and pensioners.This includes a 5% hike by the Himachal Pradesh government, 3% DA hikes each by the Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Punjab, Arunachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Gujarat governments, 2.5% increase by the Karnataka government, and 2% increases by the Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala governments.Here's a look at the latest DA and DR hikes, who's eligible and how much hike has been approved by each government.Jharkhand hikes DA, DR by 3%The Jharkhand state government on Wednesday hiked DA and DR by 3 percentage points for employees and pensioners, respectively, from 60% to to 63%, PTI reported officials stated.The raise will benefit around 3 lakh state government employees and pensioners, the officials said."The hike will be effective from July 1," as per Vandana Dadel, Additional Chief Secretary of Cabinet Secretariat and Vigilance Department.The decision was taken at a meeting of the state cabinet chaired by Chief Minister Hemant Soren, where 41 proposals were approved, including ₹37.36 crore for construction of a degree college at Vishrampur in Palamu district.Mizoram hikes DA, regularises contract staffThe Mizoram state government on Tuesday announced a four percentage-point hike in DA for its employees, raising it from 46% to 50% with effect from December 1, an official said.Notably, the state had hiked DA for employees from 36% to 44% in November 2025, followed by another increase to 46% with effect from April 1. The decision was taken at a cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Lalduhoma here, as per another PTI report.Further, the state cabinet approved doubling DA for contractual employees from 10% to 20%, effective December 1; and also approved the regularisation of contractual employees who have completed more than 10 years of service and provisional employees who have served for over 14 years, the official said.Upgradation of the pay level of District Fisheries Development Officers from Level 10A to Level 11 was also given the nod, among other proposals.Odisha hikes DA by 3%The Odisha government has hiked DA and DR for state employees and pensioners, respectively, by 3%, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced on Tuesday PTI reported.Around 8.5 lakh Odisha government employees and pensioners will benefit from the raise, officials said. The components have been increased from 60% to 63%, coming into effect retrospectively from July 1, it added.The increased DA will be paid in cash along with the salary for the month of November 2026, as per a statement from the CM's Office.(With inputs from PTI)

headline: Forest rights, unviable soils, and the agri-trap
content: By bringing right-holder families out of isolated forest interiors and settling them in better, contiguous regions, the State can deliver genuine social mobility. This approach can provide to the FRA beneficiaries direct access to healthcare, education, and stable employment while allowing the degraded forest plots to naturally regenerateThe Forest Rights Act 2006 (FRA) was passed with the objective of recognising the forest rights on forest lands, targeting the statutorily defined Forest Dwelling Scheduled Tribes (FDSTs) and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (OTFDs) who, as mentioned in the preamble itself, have been residing in such forests for generations but whose rights could not be recorded. Recently, FAO’s district-level soil mapping has been used to declare the crop suitability of forest land having Individual Forest Rights (IFR). Considering the associated factors linked with intensive farming, the proposal to develop the IFR lands into oilseed and pulse production clusters with market linkages and institutional credit across forest lands with Individual Forest Rights (IFR) of ‘self-cultivation’ under Section 3(1)(a) of the FRA, however, presents an ecological and economic paradox.While the intention to uplift the FRA’s beneficiaries appears progressive on paper, the proposed framework rests on flawed agrarian economics and a troubling obliviousness of forest ecology. Anchoring FDSTs and OTFDs to isolated, refractory forest patches under the banner of agricultural development creates, prima facie, a deep economic vulnerability for them, a situation of permanent human-wildlife conflict, and an inescapable trap of overall ecological destruction. The spatial and economic reality of the forest lands under IFR of ‘self-cultivation’ is that these plots are predominantly tiny, highly fragmented micro-holdings occupied historically for subsistence. Both before and after Independence, arable lands were systematically diverted for farming and infrastructure-a practice the National Forest Policy of 1952 sought to halt by asserting the forest’s intrinsic right to land.Repeated waves of forest encroachment regularisation, however, continued even on the inherently refractory soils in forest areas. FRA essentially had to recognise the forest rights that escaped all such attempts. As regards the average size, a 2013 study of randomly selected 36,600 cases in Maharashtra showed that 43% of IFR recognitions averaged a mere 1.3 acres.Forest-interior intensive farming would threaten biodiversity, and agrochemicals would pollute water pathways and food webs, poisoning non-target flora and fauna, while increased human footprint in forests would escalate human-wildlife conflict. This dynamic is already starkly evident in the states of Kerala, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Assam, Odisha, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh, showing increasing trends over recent years. It has led to an alarming rise in fatal animal attacks, widespread crop raiding, and retaliatory wildlife killings.The administrative push to build scattered support systems-such as micro-irrigation, storage units, and road networks-for lakhs of isolated, pockmarked plots across forest interiors is both economically inefficient and ecologically damaging. Worse still, bringing resource-poor forest dwellers into credit-dependent farming regimes will expose them to severe financial distress. Indian agrarian reality is already plagued by input-cost inflation, debt traps, and climate volatility, factors directly linked to the ongoing crisis of farmer suicides in central India.Forcing FRA beneficiaries to rely on institutional credit and volatile market prices for survival on marginal land threatens to replicate the tragic debt cycles inside tribal belts. As soil productivity inevitably declines over time due to nutrient depletion, impoverished farmers will face immense pressure to clear adjacent forest lands to maintain yields. This will, apart from criminalising their livelihood, expand the size and number of pockmarks across the landscape, converting dense forest ecosystems into fragmented islands of poverty-stricken communities.The approach of using FAO’s district-level soil mapping data for declaring crop suitability of plots inside forest areas is logically flawed, as coarse regional soil data cannot predict interior forest land’s suitability. Ironically, India’s own land classification strictly separates agricultural from forest lands using realistic, site-specific parameters to boost agrarian output safely. It should, however, be noted that categorising forest plots erroneously as high-yield farmland risks a dangerous triggering of land conflict, deforestation, and diversion of forest areas. The environmental fallout of action taken to convert these plots into high-yield agricultural nodes would be catastrophic. Any introduction of intensive farming, localised irrigation schemes, processing units, and transport links would disrupt contiguous forest canopy, causing severe habitat fragmentation. Unlike past encroachment regularisation drives, the FRA process lacks any focus on buffer restrictions near water bodies and on slopes. As per a 2013 Maharashtra study, 15% of cases lie within 50 meters of streams, and many on slopes above 10%. In hilly areas and Himalayan regions, intensive farming on fragile slopes and riverbeds would accelerate soil erosion, landslides, and siltation during the rainy season, threatening both agriculture and the core forest ecosystems. The examples of extensive damage in the Western Ghats, the Himalayan states of Himachal and Uttarakhand, Kerala, Assam, and Maharashtra, triggered by land-breaking, are indicative.This ecological threat is compounded by widespread procedural abuse in the implementation of FRA, where ineligible occupants exploit Section 4(5) to prevent their eviction; District Level Committees, the final authorities in the matter, continue to do mass irregular recognitions without proper scrutiny. Just to quote some cases, IFRs are granted in hundreds of cases to more than one applicant on the same plots in Bhadradri Kothagudem District and on thousands of podu land plots by rejecting satellite image-based evidence in Telangana. IFRs have been granted on exactly one-acre plots to more than 66 per cent of applicants in Balgan Taluka of Nasik in Maharashtra, and exactly two-acre plots have been granted to a large number of claimants in the same district. Again, Community Forest Resource Rights have been granted over 1.9 crore acres of the Forest Department’s forest area in the country without meeting legal criteria. Extending state benefits in such unauthorised cases to claimants constitutes a double illegality that misallocates public funds and legitimises unlawful action.Historically, forest communities, with far smaller populations compared to today, depended not just on sedentary crop farming alone; their sustained survival included a diversified portfolio of minor forest produce (MFP) collection, livestock grazing, seasonal wage labour, and foraging. Any attempt to drive their socio-economic mobility today by forcing intensive agriculture onto IFR plots, expanding CFRRs onto ineligible forest lands, and exceeding legal limits for MFP and grazing will, in the long run, simply overburden the exhausted forests and trap the huge population in a cycle of diminishing returns. Intensive agriculture, after all, is a form of "resource mining" in contrast to a forest ecosystem that preserves ecological stability and supports broader landscapes far beyond forest borders.Policymakers must adopt a sustainable and ecologically grounded approach towards the development of the beneficiaries of FRA rather than anchoring vulnerable populations precariously to broken, isolated plots exposed to extreme weather, unviable yields, and relentless crop raiding in the name of unlocking the agri-potential of FRA lands. The true solution lies in offering fair, attractive, and voluntary resettlement & rehabilitation packages, keeping the ‘nature’ and ‘extent’ of their forest rights intact on the alternate site. Till the time that is done, the right holders should be encouraged to cultivate local minor forest produce, including medicinal plants and go for horticultural and silvicultural species rather than intensive monoculture or commercial crop expansion.Sustainable development requires respecting ecological thresholds, protecting forest health, respecting nature’s intrinsic right to exist and transitioning toward sustainable, non-extractive economic alternatives outside the overburdened forest ecosystem. By bringing right-holder families out of isolated forest interiors and settling them in better, contiguous regions, the State can deliver genuine social mobility. This approach can provide to the FRA beneficiaries direct access to healthcare, education, appropriate infrastructure, and stable employment while allowing the degraded forest plots to naturally regenerate and heal wildlife habitats and safeguarding simultaneously the national biodiversity for generations to come.Forest-interior intensive farming would threaten biodiversity, and agrochemicals would pollute water pathways and food webs, poisoning non-target flora and fauna, while increased human footprint in forests would escalate human-wildlife conflictThe writers are former PCCFs of UP and Maharashtra; Views presented are personal.

headline: MP Scraps 2-Child Norm Rule For Govt Jobs, 30,000 School Teachers To Benefit
content: Bhopal: The Madhya Pradesh cabinet on Wednesday approved the proposal to end the two-child norm for government jobs that had been in place for two and half decades.The decision was taken at the special ‘Destination Cabinet’ meeting, held under the chairmanship of chief minister Mohan Yadav at Gandhi Sagar in Madhya Pradesh’s Mandsaur district. Amendments to Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961 and Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965 were approved by the cabinet to waive the two-child norm policy for the government employees and seekers of government jobs. Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1961 provides that candidates with more than two children are ineligible for government jobs. Similarly, Madhya Pradesh Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1965 provides that government employees having more than two children will be treated as misconduct. The two-child norm policy had been enforced in Madhya Pradesh since January 26, 2001. Official sources said that disciplinary proceedings, currently pending against around 30,000 government school teachers, will be dropped following the cabinet decision. However, final disciplinary orders already passed will not be reopened. Three other states, Chhattisgarh, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh, have already dropped the two-child norm for government jobs. Andhra Pradesh has announced a direct cash incentive of Rs 30,000 for the birth of a third child and Rs 40,000 for a fourth child. Andhra Pradesh chief minister N Chandrababu Naidu declared the policy at a public meeting in Srikakulam district on May 26.

headline: Bhopal Fake Call Centre Extortion Racket Targeting Sarpanchs Across 8 States Under SIT Probe, 618 Registers
content: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh): Nagpur rural police have constituted a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by an additional superintendent of police to investigate the high-profile extortion racket allegedly operated through fake call centres in Bhopal. The racket busted on Tuesday targeted village sarpanchs and other panchayat representatives in eight states with callers posing as journalists and threatening to expose alleged corruption in their respective panchayats to extort money.Nagpur rural police additional SP Anil Mhaske said the court granted police remand to the four arrested women till November 21. Investigators will question them about 618 registers recovered during the operation, which contain details of panchayat members from eight states. Meanwhile, the investigation in Bhopal has also widened, with several other people allegedly linked to the arrested women coming under the police lens.Police are examining how the information was collected, how it was used to identify potential targets and how many people listed in the registers have already been subjected to extortion. Investigators are also questioning the suspects about other members of the network and their respective roles in running the operation.The racket was busted in a joint operation by Nagpur police and TT Nagar police. A Nagpur police team arrived in Bhopal and traced the callers to three illegal call centres operating from Harsh Vardhan Nagar, Nishatpura and MP Nagar.About 35 women were reportedly working at the three call centres. Police arrested four women including the alleged mastermind Monika Lal Singh Suryavanshi (28). The other suspects have been identified as Neha Lal Singh (23), Akshara Milind Ark (21) and Komal Mohan More (23).Police served notices to the other women working at the centres. The racket allegedly targeted sarpanchs from Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh and Jharkhand. The callers allegedly posed as journalists and threatened to publish reports exposing corruption in village panchayats unless the representatives paid them money.Level up your brain the fun way. headline: Back from Dubai for Diwali, 28-year-old dies mysteriously
content: Ludhiana: A 28-year-old man who returned from Dubai around a month ago to celebrate Diwali with his family died under mysterious circumstances in Machhiwara Wednesday, with his family alleging that his maternal cousin injected him with narcotics.Gagandeep Singh of Mangat Colony was found unconscious near the old vegetable market Wednesday morning. He was rushed to hospital, where doctors declared him dead.According to the family, Gagandeep had left home around 6.30am. They were later informed that he was lying unconscious near the vegetable market. The family claimed they noticed injection marks on his arm at the hospital and alleged that his maternal cousin had administered drugs to him.Police, however, said the exact cause of death would be known only after the post-mortem report.Machhiwara SHO SI Charanjit Singh said the body had been sent for post-mortem examination and the deceased’s maternal cousin had been arrested on the basis of the family’s allegations. Legal proceedings were being initiated.Police are also investigating the source of the suspected drugs and said further arrests could follow depending on the findings.Gagandeep was married and is survived by two young children. headline: Where science meets tradition, vet varsity gets a Punjabi makeover
content: Ludhiana: It was a day when textbooks and laboratories took a back seat as kavishri rang out, mehndi patterns took shape and the traditional lambi gutt shared space with cartoons and collages at Guru Angad Dev Veterinary and Animal Sciences University.The third day of the university’s 15th Youth Festival, YUV-TARANG 2026, turned into a celebration of Punjab’s cultural roots, with students combining traditional art forms with contemporary creative expression.Kavishri, Punjab’s powerful tradition of rhythmic poetic recitation, provided the cultural high point as students brought the state’s oral heritage alive through energetic performances. Mehndi and lambi gutt competitions added colour to the festivities, while cartoons and collages gave participants a canvas to engage with contemporary themes and social issues.Vice-Chancellor JPS Gill said the competitions reflected Punjab’s cultural richness and gave students an opportunity to celebrate tradition, creativity and collective identity.Director Students’ Welfare JS Hundal said kavishri helped connect youngsters with their cultural roots, while cartoon and collage-making encouraged artistic expression and engagement with social issues.In kavishri, the College of Veterinary Science, Ludhiana, took the top spot, followed by the College of Dairy and Food Science Technology and Veterinary Polytechnic, Kaljharani, Bathinda.Samarpreet Singh won the cartoon-making contest, while Prabhjot Kaur topped the collage competition. headline: Buddha Dariya doesn’t need new plans, enforce existing laws: Activists
content: Ludhiana: Calling for enforcement of existing environmental laws rather than fresh policies and technological fixes, Kale Pani da Morcha and the Public Action Committee (PAC) Thursday questioned the govt’s approach to cleaning Buddha Dariya, alleging that three common effluent treatment plants (CETPs) continue to violate pollution norms.In a joint communication to Rajya Sabha member Balbir Singh Seechewal, who heads the Punjab govt-appointed committee on Buddha Dariya, the organisations sought a meeting with the panel and a copy of its report, if completed. They said the committee had reportedly been given 15 days to submit its findings after being constituted towards the end of Oct.The organisations argued that enforcing existing laws should come before announcing new schemes, treatment plants or technological interventions. Fresh investments and grants would achieve little, they said, if illegal discharge of effluents continued.Citing findings of central and state agencies, they alleged that all three CETPs along Buddha Dariya continued to violate environmental norms despite being established with financial assistance from the Centre and state.They also flagged what they described as poor recovery of environmental compensation imposed by the Punjab Pollution Control Board (PPCB), saying a substantial amount remained outstanding and had been referred to the Ludhiana deputy commissioner for recovery.Highlighting the impact on the Sutlej, the organisations cited environment ministry findings showing dissolved oxygen levels falling from 8.5mg per litre upstream of the Buddha Dariya confluence to 1.5mg per litre downstream. They claimed the river also failed to meet bathing-water quality standards after the confluence.“None of this requires a new study, policy or technology. The conditions already exist and the pollution control board has the necessary powers. What is missing is enforcement,” they said.The organisations also alleged attempts to divert attention from the pollution issue, citing the recent arrests of Kale Pani da Morcha members Lakha Singh Sidhana, Mohinder Pal Loomba and Amitoj Mann.The Buddha Dariya pollution matter is pending before the NGT’s principal bench in New Delhi, with the next hearing scheduled for Jan 8, 2027.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ludhiana | Silver Rate in Ludhiana | Bank Holidays in Ludhiana | Public Holidays in Ludhiana | Petrol Price in Ludhiana | Diesel Price in Ludhiana | CNG Price in Ludhiana | LPG Price in LudhianaStay updated with the latest Ludhiana news. headline: Warring says Rahul Gandhi will consider his recommendations for Punjab poll tickets
content: CHANDIGARH: Former Punjab Congress president and Ludhiana MP Amarinder Singh Raja Warring on Thursday said that Rahul Gandhi had given him considerable importance in the party and would consider his recommendations for ticket distribution in the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.Warring also announced an 'Insaaf March' in Ludhiana on November 21, accusing the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government of failing to curb gangsterism, extortion and drug trafficking. The march will demand accountability over the state's law and order situation and other pressing issues.The march will begin from Ludhiana (Central), with similar marches planned across all Assembly constituencies in the city before being extended to other parts of Punjab, including Zira, Bathinda, Mansa and Muktsar."The final call on tickets to aspirants would, however, be taken by Rahul Gandhi, Malikarjun Kharge and Sachin Pilot, in-charge of Punjab affairs," he said.Warring said the march was part of the "Punjab Mangda Hisab" campaign launched by Gandhi from Sangrur on November 4.Addressing differences within the state Congress leadership, particularly as the 'Jawani Sambhal Yatra' led by former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi concluded in Khanna on Thursday, Warring said in a lighter vein, "It is good for us, we are getting much attention of the media on the issue, and we are getting a lot of publicity."He added, "You never know I can be part of the cycle yatra in the coming days as Channi would plan more yatras."Asked about the absence of photographs of some leaders from the 'Insaaf Yatra' posters, Warring said there could be differences of opinion among party members but that the Congress would present a united front in the Assembly elections. "I have no enmity with anyone," he said.Warring alleged that 170 murder cases had been reported in Ludhiana between 2022 and 2024, questioning the government's ability to protect residents. He said traders and industrialists were increasingly receiving extortion threats from gangsters, with several business owners reluctant to approach the police for fear of retaliation..'You could smell alcohol on his breath in Parliament': Rahul Gandhi targets CM Mann over drug menace in Punjab.He said Ludhiana, one of Punjab's major industrial centres, was suffering from inadequate government support and an atmosphere of insecurity that was affecting commercial activity."The AAP government, which came to power in the name of change, has betrayed the people of Punjab," Warring said, accusing Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's government of failing to fulfil its election promises.He also claimed that the drug trade had increased fourfold under the AAP government and questioned the effectiveness of its 'Yudh Nashean Virudh' campaign. Expressing concern over the reported emergence of dangerous synthetic substances, including so-called zombie drugs, he alleged that people speaking out against drug trafficking were facing threats and violence.Referring to the killing of Parvinder Jhotta, Warring alleged that he was shot dead for raising his voice against drugs. He also cited an earlier incident in which seven houses were allegedly set on fire following objections to drug trafficking.Citing the killings of singer Sidhu Moosewala and several others, including kabaddi players, Warring said the incidents highlighted serious concerns over public safety."The government cannot evade responsibility for the deteriorating law and order situation, rising gangsterism and the drug menace in Punjab," he said..Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: On Congress Panel For Punjab Election Tickets, Gandhis' Trusted Giant Slayer From UP
content: Of the 42 leaders the Congress has named to help pick its candidates in Punjab, 41 have built their politics in the state. The 42nd is Kishori Lal Sharma, the MP from Uttar Pradesh's Amethi, who left Ludhiana in 1983 to work for Rajiv Gandhi and has stayed close to the Gandhi family ever since. By his own account, his Aadhaar and voter ID remained in Ludhiana. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge named the family loyalist, who avenged Rahul Gandhi's 2019 defeat by winning against the BJP's Smriti Irani in 2024, to the key panel on Wednesday evening. State Congress president Pargat Singh chairs the committee, which includes Charanjit Singh Channi, Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, Partap Singh Bajwa, and veteran Ambika Soni. The party's central in-charge of Punjab is an ex-officio member. Kishori Lal Sharma's appointment among leaders otherwise rooted in Punjab for decades comes when the Gandhis have struggled to stem factionalism in the state unit. The Pradesh Election Committee is the state-level body in the Congress's candidate selection process for the 117-member Punjab Assembly. This panel recommends names to a screening committee appointed by the AICC, which shortlists candidates for the Central Election Committee, chaired by the party president, to finalise. The ruling AAP has declared over 70 candidates so far, while the SAD and BJP are in talks to get back together.

headline: Ludhiana: Climate change making weed control harder, say experts | Hindustan Times
content: Climate change, emerging weed species and herbicide resistance are posing fresh challenges to Indian agriculture, scientists warned at Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) on Wednesday, calling for affordable and technology-driven ways to tackle the problem. Citing an ICAR report, Indian Society of Weed Science (ISWS) president TK Das said weeds cause annual economic losses of up to $12.6 billion in India.Addressing the inaugural session of the four-day fourth International Weed Conference (IWC-2026), PAU vice-chancellor Harvinder Singh Dhaliwal said, “Changing climatic conditions are leading to the emergence of new weeds and making their management increasingly complex.” Stressing the need for research into changing weed patterns and climate-smart, environmentally sustainable technologies, he said weed-management solutions must be affordable, accessible, convenient and practical for farmers. He also emphasised that technological interventions should protect crop productivity while supporting natural resource conservation and environmental protection.Citing the 2026 report of the ICAR-Directorate of Weed Research (DWR), Das called for greater research into climate resilience, soil health, water-related challenges and herbicide resistance. He also advocated the development of organic and biological herbicides to improve farm productivity and profitability.Guest of honour professor Baruch Rubin, an expert in herbicide resistance and weed biology from The Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Israel, stressed the need for stronger international scientific collaboration to address emerging challenges in weed management.The conference, themed ‘Technological Innovations in Weed Management for Climate-Resilient Sustainable Agri-Food Systems’, brought together more than 500 scientists, international delegates, students, young researchers and industry representatives from 10 countries. Organised by the ISWS in collaboration with PAU, ICAR-DWR, Jabalpur, and the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR), New Delhi, the event will deliberate on integrated weed management, herbicide resistance, biological control, precision weed management, artificial intelligence and weed control in conservation agriculture.MS Bhullar, director of extension education and chairperson of the local organising committee, said the discussions were expected to generate ideas for sustainable weed-control technologies.The ISWS also presented national and international honours, including lifetime achievement awards, fellowships, gold medals and best scientist awards for 2024-25. Two publications, Biology and Management of Weeds in Asia and Africa and 57 Years of Research in Weed Management, were released at the inaugural session.

headline: Kejriwal cites Chouhan’s praise for Punjab farmers to counter BJP’s stubble-burning claims
content: Chandigarh: AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Wednesday cited Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s remarks praising Punjab’s farmers for reducing stubble burning to question the BJP’s criticism of the state over pollution.Sharing a video of Chouhan on social media, Kejriwal said the minister had acknowledged a “historic decline” in farm fires in Punjab. He accused the BJP and Congress of continuing to blame the state’s farmers despite the reduction. “The Union Minister himself is admitting that Punjab’s farmers have significantly reduced stubble burning. Unfortunately, he and his party, in cahoots with Congress, keep hurling abuse at Punjab’s farmers day and night as part of dirty politics,” Kejriwal said.In a separate press statement, he reiterated that Chouhan had acknowledged a significant reduction in stubble burning in Punjab. headline: Karnataka to open India’s first government Sports Technology CoE
content: Bengaluru The Karnataka government has decided to set up a Centre of Excellence (CoE) for Sports Technologies, the first such facility in the country. To this end, the government has on Thursday signed a Letter of Intent with Amagi Media Labs, a cloud-based software-as-a-service firm based in Bengaluru, to establish India’s first government-backed Sports Technology CoE in the city. The CoE is expected to integrate DeepTech, scientific research and industry expertise to strengthen the country’s sporting ecosystem. While the State government would provide seed funding and infrastructure facilitation, the operational roles would be handled independently by industry professionals. Foundation pillars According to official details, the proposed CoE will operate on three foundational pillars. The first pillar, ‘Core Technology and Research Areas’, will focus on sports analytics, DeepTech, biomechanics, health and life sciences, and sports hardware and electronics. The second pillar, ‘Athlete Development’, will cover virtual training simulations, injury prevention and rehabilitation, sports psychology, talent identification, assistive technology, coaching, and initiatives supporting women in sports. The third pillar, ‘Cross-Cutting Ecosystem Enablers’, will drive applied research, product testing, skilling and institutional partnerships. Describing the model as a unique experiment, IT&BT and Home Minister Priyank Kharge stated, “The facility will be run by the industry, for the industry and for the sports fraternity.’’ He also expressed optimism that more corporate partners would soon join the initiative and make it big. More specific deliverables, governance structures, resource allocations, and so on would be finalised between the State government and Amagi Media Labs through subsequent definitive agreements. The Minister pointed to Karnataka’s track record of running over 20 industry-partnered CoEs, including C-CAMP, Bengaluru Bioinnovation Centre, ARTpark and CISEC, which have collectively generated intellectual property valued at over ₹13,000 crore. Market value The Indian sports market was valued at ₹1.99 lakh crore ($20.6 billion) in 2026 and is growing at an annual rate of 12%-14%. According to a KPMG forecast, the industry is expected to reach $42.42 billion by 2030-31. “India’s sports ecosystem is projected to grow in double digits in the coming years, presenting a strategic opportunity for the State,” Mr. Kharge stated.

headline: World Health Organisation team reviews Telangana’s NCD control initiatives
content: HYDERABAD Representatives from World Health Organisation (WHO) visited health centres in Telangana on Thursday, November 19, to review the healthcare services being provided and assess the State’s initiatives to control hypertension and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs). The teams visited health centres in Kuknoor Palli, Mulugu, Marpaddaga and Rayavaram villages in Siddipet district, besides the Alwal Health Centre in Hyderabad. During the visits, they interacted with medical staff and enquired about the healthcare facilities, services available to patients and measures being implemented to prevent and manage NCDs. The teams reviewed the diagnostic services provided through the Telangana Diagnostic Hub and assessed the functioning and utilisation of the Telangana NCD Portal, developed by the State Health Department to record and monitor public health information. The WHO representatives appreciated Telangana’s initiatives in NCD control, the adoption of digital technology in healthcare delivery and the provision of services at the primary healthcare level, said a release from the health department.

headline: Telecom Manufacturing Zone, Gwalior Gains Momentum with Distribution of Letters of Intent to 25 Companies
content: The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, Government of India, in collaboration with the Government of Madhya Pradesh, organised a Letter of Intent (LoI) Distribution Ceremony for 25 companies investing in the Telecom Manufacturing Zone (TMZ), Gwalior, in Bhopal today. The event marked an important milestone in advancing India's vision of becoming a global hub for telecom manufacturing, innovation and technology development. The ceremony was graced by Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav and Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia. Senior officials of the Government of India and the Government of Madhya Pradesh, along with representatives from the telecom and electronics industries, participated in the programme. The programme also marked the announcement of Phase-II of the Telecom Manufacturing Zone, signalling a significant step towards expanding the zone's manufacturing ecosystem and strengthening investment opportunities in the telecom and electronics sectors. Addressing the gathering, Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia said “India has established itself as a global leader in telecom services. However, the time has now come for the next paradigm shift in the telecom industry. We must move from being a services nation to becoming a product nation. It is the responsibility of the Government of India to create an ecosystem that enables industry to establish manufacturing facilities and grow. The Minister further emphasized, “Hon'ble Prime Minister's vision has always been that there was a time when India depended on the world, but today India is self-reliant. The day is not far when the world will depend on India. We must work towards making this vision a reality in the coming decade. This is India's time, and this is the time for Madhya Pradesh." The Hon'ble Chief Minister of Madhya Pradesh, Dr. Mohan Yadav, highlighted “This is the first time in the history of India that we have been able to build a zone dedicated to telecom sector. It is the best example of how the Central and State Government work in tandem for rapid development of industry. For this zone, we have given approval to 170 acres of land through the Cabinet.” The programme featured a presentation on the Telecom Manufacturing Zone project and its development roadmap by the Government of Madhya Pradesh. Industry representatives also shared their perspectives on investment opportunities and industry participation.

The Government of Chhattisgarh, in coordination with the Ministry of Tribal Affairs, is working on a Comprehensive Development Plan for the Bastar region, covering seven districts with a focus on improving the quality of life of tribal communities. headline: Haryana Roadways bus veers off road while trying to save scooty-borne girls in Patiala, 5 injured
content: A Haryana Roadways bus veered off the road while trying to save two girls riding an electric scooty near the Hamjheri Bypass T-point on the Jakhal-Patran road in Patiala district on Thursday morning, leaving five people, including the driver and conductor, injured.The incident took place when the bus was travelling from Fatehabad to Patran in Patiala district.According to the bus conductor, two girls riding an electric scooty suddenly came in front of the bus near the Hamjheri Bypass T-point. In an attempt to save them, the driver lost control of the steering, causing the bus to veer off the road.The injured were identified as bus driver Naveen and conductor Vinod Kumar, both residents of Bhuna tehsil in Fatehabad district, Haryana.The two injured passengers were Amar Chauhan (30), a resident of Fatehabad, and Nachhattar Singh (64), a resident of Ratia, Haryana. Kajal, one of the girls riding the scooty, was also injured in the mishap.The driver and conductor were admitted to Noor Hospital, Patran, while Kajal was taken to Durga Dal Charitable Hospital, Patran. The two injured passengers were initially taken to the Community Health Centre (CHC), Patran, from where they were referred to Government Rajindra Medical College and Hospital, Patiala, for further treatment.The local police have begun an investigation into the incident.

headline: Bailey bridge on Patiala-Sangrur-Bathinda highway collapses, 2 trucks left dangling
content: A Bailey bridge over the Bhakra canal on the Patiala-Sangrur-Bathinda National Highway suddenly collapsed on Thursday morning, leaving two trucks dangling in the broken structure. One of the trucks also caught fire. No casualties were reported in the incident.However, the drivers of both trucks sustained minor injuries.The incident occurred near Passiana village in the early hours when the two trucks, reportedly overloaded with sand, were crossing the bridge.Preliminary findings suggest that the bridge collapsed due to excessive weight, possibly beyond the prescribed load limit. However, the exact cause will be ascertained by technical experts.Following the collapse, the two trucks got trapped in the broken structure and remained suspended over the canal. Meanwhile, water from the Bhakra canal started flowing over the collapsed portion of the bridge.A fire tender was rushed to the spot to douse the fire in one of the trucks. Rescue teams from the district administration, along with police and fire personnel, reached the site to manage the situation and carry out relief and rescue operations.Traffic on the affected stretch of the highway has been halted and diverted to the other side.It may be mentioned that the National Highway was completed in 2016, and the bridge was constructed around the same time. Its collapse barely 10 years later has raised questions over the structure's durability and construction quality.This correspondent tried to contact District Magistrate Himanshu Jain for his official version, but he did not respond to calls.

headline: AAP releases list of 21 for Patiala MC repoll
content: The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) on Wednesday released its list of candidates for 21 wards for the Municipal Corporation re-elections. Nine candidates were named on Monday. His credibility among the masses must have been taken into account while naming the candidates,” he maintained.The candidates announced for the 21 wards are Sonia Das (Ward 1), Ranjit Singh (Ward 32), Geeta Rani (Ward 33), Tejinder Mehta (Ward 34), Harpreet Singh (Ward 36), Renu Bala (Ward 37), Harpal Juneja (Ward 38), Sanjeev Kakkar (Ward 40), Amanpreet Kaur (Ward 41), Meenakshi Kashyap (Ward 43), Gursharan Singh (Ward 44), Jyoti (Ward 45), Rajesh Gupta (Ward 46), Rajesh Kumar (Ward 48), Harman Sandhu (Ward 50), Kiran Ahuja (Ward 51), Sagar (Ward 52), Rupinder Kaur (Ward 53), Kanwaljit Kaur (Ward 55), Rupali Arora (Ward 57) and Sukhdev Singh (Ward 58).Among the candidates, Sanjeev Kakkar, Meenakshi Kashyap, Jyoti, Rajesh Gupta, Rupinder Kaur, Rupali Arora and Sukhdev Singh are among the new faces fielded by the party.It may be mentioned that AAP has also fielded Chairman of the Pepsu Road Transport Corporation (PRTC) Harpal Juneja from Ward No. 38 while District Planning Board Chairman Tejinder Mehta will contest from Ward No. 34. headline: Malwa civic polls a litmus test for parties ahead of Punjab Assembly elections
content: With the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections round the corner, the civic elections scheduled for November 28 have emerged as a litmus test for all political parties in the state’s politically sensitive Malwa region. Each political party is testing its mettle in these polls being held in 52 wards of three local bodies.Since this will be the last electoral contest before the Assembly elections, the polls are being viewed as an opportunity by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Congress, BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) to demonstrate their political strength and organisational preparedness. Interestingly, in spite of the buzz over the SAD-BJP alliance, they are contesting these civic polls independently. Since the BJP top leaders are giving mixed signals over the alliance and the SAD leaders are staying mum, the electorate in these areas will be judging their candidates on their individual and party merits.Fresh elections in 52 wards of the Patiala Municipal Corporation and the municipal councils of Bagha Purana and Dharamkot have been necessitated following the intervention of the Supreme Court. Polling will be held in 30 wards of Patiala, 15 of Bagha Purana and seven of Dharamkot.A total of 172 nominations have been received till today, with Patiala accounting for the maximum at 105, followed by 47 in Bagha Purana and 20 in Dharamkot.With this being the last electoral contest before the grand finale in 2027, all major political parties are keen to outperform their rivals. A strong showing in these elections is expected to give a morale boost to party cadres and strengthen their confidence ahead of the Assembly polls. All major parties have announced their candidates and are mobilising their organisational machinery for the contest.For the ruling AAP, the elections will provide an opportunity to gauge public response to its performance over the past four-and-a-half years. The party has been highlighting its development initiatives and governance record. The Opposition, on the other hand, will seek to turn the civic polls into a referendum on the state government’s performance and raise issues concerning urban voters.The Patiala Municipal Corporation elections are particularly significant, with 30 of its 60 wards going to the polls. The contest also has implications for several senior political functionaries in Patiala whose wards are among those where fresh elections are being held. In fact, it has become an interesting political battle between AAP and BJP.The BJP is expected to highlight the performance of the Centre, while the AAP will seek to defend its governance record. The Congress and SAD will also look to use the opportunity to gain political ground in urban areas.The results will be closely watched not just as an indicator of the relative organisational strength and public support to each party, but also to test the choppy waters in the politically volatile Malwa.All three local bodies going to the polls are located in Malwa, which has 69 of the 117 Assembly constituencies. Thus, the impact of the elections will be the maximum in this region, particularly in Patiala and Moga districts.

headline: YouTube Takes Down Over 19,000 Pro-Indonesia Government Channels, Here's Why
content: YouTube has removed more than 19,000 YouTube channels linked to Indonesia in a single quarter for sharing content supporting the country’s government, bringing attention to the use of online platforms to influence public opinion. The removals point to a rise in coordinated online activity in Indonesia, where YouTube has a large audience and plays a role in political discussions. According to a Bloomberg report, Google terminated 19,372 YouTube channels between July and September 2026. The figure marks a sharp increase compared with the previous quarters. The company had removed 437 channels sharing pro-government content between April and June, while 3,598 channels were taken down during the first three months of the year. The figures were shared in Google’s quarterly bulletin on influence operations, which tracks accounts and networks removed for violating its policies against coordinated activities. Sharp Rise in Channel Removals Indonesia had not featured frequently in Google’s influence operation reports since the company began publishing them in 2020. However, the number of channel removals linked to the country started increasing in the second half of 2025. The latest figures come after Indonesia witnessed nationwide anti-government protests in late August 2025. Demonstrations were triggered by public anger over benefits given to lawmakers, economic concerns and allegations of police brutality. The protests also created a major challenge for President Prabowo Subianto’s administration. Google had removed 445 channels sharing pro-government content in September 2025. However, the company has not established any link between those removals and the protests. Who Was Behind The Campaigns? Google’s latest report, published on October 30, said the removed channels mainly shared Indonesian-language content supporting Prabowo’s government. Some accounts also posted material criticising people who opposed the administration. The company has not disclosed who operated or funded these networks. It has also not confirmed whether the accounts had direct links to the Indonesian government or how many people watched their videos. The number of removals should also not be treated as a measure of how many people were exposed to the campaigns. The figures represent Google’s enforcement actions and do not necessarily reflect the actual size or reach of the activity. A representative of Indonesia’s Government Communication Agency did not immediately respond to Bloomberg’s request for comment. Google also did not respond to requests for information. YouTube’s Reach In Indonesia Indonesia is among YouTube’s largest markets worldwide. The platform has an estimated advertising audience of 155 million people in the country, making it the third-largest market after India and the US. With such a large user base, YouTube remains an important platform for political communication in Indonesia, which is the world’s fourth-most populous country. The latest removals also highlight Google’s continued efforts to identify and take down coordinated networks that use its services to influence online discussions.
