headline: Delhi To Launch Student Mental Health Policy Today; 1 Counsellor Proposed Per 500 School Students
content: The Delhi government is set to introduce a Mental Well-Being Policy aimed at addressing the emotional and psychological health of children and young people up to 29 years of age, including those outside the formal education system. It has now proposed appointing one counsellor for every 500 school students and one for every 100 students in higher education institutions, reported Indian Express. Education Minister Ashish Sood had earlier stated that the proposed policy will cover CM SHRI schools, government and government-aided schools, private educational institutions, higher education institutions and children with special needs. The initiative is expected to bring around 23 lakh school students under a common mental health support system. This includes nearly 15 lakh students in Directorate of Education-run schools and around eight lakh in private schools. Children with Special Needs and young people up to 29 years of age, including those outside formal education, will also be covered. Under the policy, schools and colleges will receive handbooks with structured questions, practical exercises and activities to help teachers and other staff identify early signs of emotional distress. Mental health support will involve not just teachers but also administrative, non-teaching and transport staff who regularly interact with students. The policy will follow a two-stage process, beginning with mental health assessments across schools and colleges. Students identified as requiring support may subsequently receive counselling. The policy was finalised following consultations with NITI Aayog, UNESCO, INMAS and other experts, officials said. The initiative aims to create an environment where students can discuss their emotional concerns and seek support without fear of judgement or social stigma. The policy is scheduled to be formally launch today, November 19 at the Indira Gandhi Indoor Stadium in the presence of spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar. It is part of the government’s broader effort to focus on students’ confidence, resilience and overall development alongside academic performance.

headline: BJP’s Harsh Mahajan demands Himachal minister’s apology for remarks on Rafale, Op Sindoor
content: Shimla, Nov 19 (PTI) Senior BJP leader and Rajya Sabha MP Harsh Mahajan on Thursday demanded that Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi apologise for his remarks regarding the purchase of Rafale fighter jets and their effectiveness during Operation Sindoor, which has stirred a controversy in Himachal Pradesh. Issuing a strong condemnation of the minister’s claims, Mahajan said Negi’s remarks were highly irresponsible, unfortunate and disrespectful towards the Indian armed forces. In a statement, Mahajan said Negi has made allegations of corruption without presenting “credible evidence”. “If he possesses evidence of corruption, he should place it before the appropriate authorities. Defence procurement involves sophisticated weapon systems, advanced technology, training, maintenance and logistical support. Making sweeping allegations without understanding these components reflects political irresponsibility,” Mahajan said. Negi’s remarks a day ago caused a furore in the Himachal Assembly on Thursday, with Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania expunging the minister’s remarks following a demand by the opposition BJP that the Army should not be the subject of such commentary. Mahajan, in his statement, expressed concern over Negi’s remarks questioning the effectiveness of Operation Sindoor.

headline: HP High Court Halts Section 118 Land Permissions in Solan Over Rampant Hill Cutting in Kasauli
content: HP High Court Halts Section 118 Land Permissions in Solan Over Rampant Hill Cutting in Kasauli SHIMLA, NOVEMBER 19: Taking a stern view of unchecked commercial construction and severe ecological damage in the Kasauli hills, the High Court of Himachal Pradesh on Thursday barred the state government from granting any land purchase permissions under Section 118 of the HP Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, in Solan district without prior approval from the court. A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin Chander Negi passed the interim order while hearing a suo motu Public Interest Litigation (PIL). The court stipulated that any future request for Section 118 clearance in the district must be backed by "justifiable reasons." Overruling strong objections from the state’s counsel against the interim stay, the Bench observed that successive governments over the past decades have granted permissions "unabatedly," reducing the strict provisions of Section 118 to a "dead letter" and fueling a boom in commercial flats. "Until extreme orders are passed, the State will not remedy itself," the court remarked, noting that the government had failed to get a grip on the situation or place consolidated data on record. The judicial crackdown stems from a joint inspection report submitted in person by the Sub-Divisional Officer (Civil), Kasauli, regarding massive excavation work at a property known as 'Woodvilla' in Ferozi Village on Lower Mall, Kasauli.

headline: ’51 families displaced due to disasters in Himachal Pradesh over 3 years’
content: Shimla/Dharamshala, Nov 19 (PTI) Floods and other disasters in Himachal Pradesh rendered at least 51 families homeless over the past three years, Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi said on Thursday. Negi was responding to a question raised by MLA Bhuvneshwar Gaur. According to the minister’s written reply, the allocation of land for the permanent rehabilitation of 25 affected families is pending. He said that where the use of forest land is involved, approval from the Centre is required, and such clearance is awaited. The government said that a record of families rendered landless and displaced by disasters has been compiled up to November 1. The minister said the government has issued a notification for land allocation to facilitate the permanent rehabilitation of families affected by the natural disasters that occurred during the 2023 monsoon.

headline: Himachal minister stokes row with Op Sindoor remarks; BJP says remarks echo Pakistan's language
content: NEW DELHI: Himachal Pradesh minister Jagat Singh Negi triggered a controversy on Thursday after he said that India had a "tough time" dealing with Pakistan during Operation Sindoor.During the assembly session, the BJP moved an adjournment motion to hold a debate on corruption. While addressing the House, Negi alleged massive corruption in the procurement of Rafale fighter jets, claiming India paid Rs 2,300 crore per aircraft instead of Rs 700 crore. Negi also alleged that the fighter jets "proved useless" and resulted in India "having a tough time dealing with Pakistan"."The biggest threat facing India today is corruption and the misuse of public money. That has always been a concern. Let me give you an example of corruption. An aircraft was supposed to be bought for Rs 700 crore. It was called Rafale, a very good aircraft. You bought it for Rs 2,300 crore. That is where corruption took place, because it wasn't made of silver," Negi said."And did that Rafale aircraft give Pakistan a tough time during Operation Sindoor? Instead, we were the ones who were left struggling," he added.Reacting to Negi's remarks, the BJP slammed the Himachal Pradesh minister and Congress, saying that such remarks proved that politics takes precedence over the nation for the grand old party."Congress minister Jagat Singh Negi's statement in the state assembly is extremely unfortunate and condemnable. By making such remarks about Operation Sindoor and the valour of the Indian Army, Congress has once again proved that for the party, politics takes precedence over the nation and the respect due to its soldiers," the BJP wrote in a social media post on X."Why is it that whenever the country's security and the valour of its armed forces are discussed, Congress's statements appear to echo Pakistan's language?" the party added.Himachal Pradesh leader of opposition Jairam Thakur also slammed Negi, terming his remarks absurd and irresponsible. He also urged the Speaker of the assembly to expunge his remarks from the official record."Jagat Singh Negi is known for making absurd and irresponsible statements, both inside and outside the Legislative Assembly. I fail to understand why a minister of such seniority uses such language. Yesterday, during a discussion in the Assembly, he made a very serious remark regarding the Indian Armed Forces. When one of our colleagues from the opposition pointed out to the ruling party MLAs that the Rafale fighter jets had dealt a crushing blow to the Pakistani military, Negi responded by claiming that it was not the Indian Armed Forces or the Rafale jets that had achieved this, but rather that the Indian Armed Forces themselves had been the ones to suffer a crushing defeat," Thakur said."This is recorded in the assembly proceedings. We strongly oppose this and have urged the Speaker of the assembly to ensure that these remarks are expunged from the official record," he added.BJP MLA Rakesh Jamwal also attacked Negi and said, "The way he uses language inside the assembly is concerning... He raised matters against the PM Modi-led Central government. He even questioned the country's armed forces. He made baseless remarks about Operation Sindoor and said that Rafale jets were purchased at high prices, adding that Pakistanis should have died, but Indians were losing their lives."Get the latest India News and Live updates. headline: Successive govts diluted Sec. 118, HC restrains fresh permissions in Solan
content: Taking a strong exception to successive governments diluting the stringent provisions of Section 118 of the Himachal Pradesh Tenancy and Land Reforms Act, 1972, the Himachal Pradesh High Court has restrained the State Government from granting any fresh permission under the provision in Solan district without prior approval of the Court and recording justifiable reasons. A Division Bench comprising Chief Justice Gurmeet Singh Sandhawalia and Justice Bipin Chander Negi observed that permissions under Section 118 had been granted unabatedly over the last several decades by successive governments, thereby diluting the strict statutory safeguards intended to regulate land transfers to non-agriculturists. The court observed that rampant permissions under Section 118 in Solan district were leading to extensive commercial construction in the form of flats, while the State Government had failed to get a grip on the situation. It also noted that the government had not placed any consolidated data regarding permissions granted under the Act. “Until any extreme orders are passed, the State will not remedy itself,” the Bench observed while passing the interim directions in a suo motu public interest litigation concerning environmental degradation and unregulated construction in Kasauli. The court’s intervention comes amid growing concerns over large-scale commercial development in the ecologically fragile Kasauli hills, where extensive hill cutting, tree felling and alteration of the natural terrain have been reported. In a separate but related direction, the court impleaded three real estate developers — M/s Reviera Luxury Project Five LLP, M/s Sretan Luxury Project Four LLP and M/s Jambavati Project Reality Three LLP — along with the Director of Town and Country Planning and the Secretary, Urban Development, as respondents after finding prima facie gross violations of the Hill Cutting Norms under the Policy Guidelines for Cutting, Conservation and Preservation of Hills, 2025.

headline: Illegal Drug Manufacturing Racket Busted in Himachal Pradesh, Three Detained
content: Drug control authorities from Uttar Pradesh and Himachal Pradesh have uncovered an illegal pharmaceutical manufacturing operation at Rajpura in Nalagarh, where medicines were allegedly being produced under the names of reputed pharmaceutical companies. Three people have been detained, while drug manufacturing and packaging machinery has been seized during the enforcement operation. Investigators have also identified two suspected unlicensed manufacturing facilities in the Baddi area, expanding the scope of the investigation. The operation was initiated following specific intelligence inputs received from the State Drugs Controller of the Uttar Pradesh Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) regarding suspected illegal pharmaceutical manufacturing activities in Himachal Pradesh. Acting on the information, a team comprising police personnel and drug inspectors from Uttar Pradesh travelled to Himachal Pradesh to coordinate with the state’s Drugs Control Administration. Dedicated investigation teams were subsequently formed to conduct joint enforcement operations at the suspected premises. headline: 7 Lesser-Known Indian Destinations That Feel Like Switzerland
content: Yumthang Valley: Tucked in Sikkim, Yumthang enchants visitors with sweeping alpine meadows, colorful wildflowers, hot springs, and towering snow-dusted peaks. Its peaceful, high-altitude charm feels remarkably like a quiet Swiss valley, offering serene walks and refreshing mountain air away from heavy crowds. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) Barot Valley: Winding along Ghatasani-Barot Road in Himachal Pradesh, this peaceful retreat pairs pine-clad slopes with clear river waters. Travellers love its laid-back pace, riverside camping, trout fishing, and forest trails that evoke a classic European countryside escape without commercial bustle. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) Munsiyari: Set in Uttarakhand’s Kumaon hills, Munsyari frames dramatic views of the Panchachuli peaks above green pastures. Crisp mountain air, scenic ridges, and quiet trekking paths give this offbeat gem an unmistakable alpine spirit that captivates slow-travel enthusiasts and nature photographers. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) Chitkul: Sitting near the Indo-Tibet border in Himachal Pradesh, Chitkul charms travelers with traditional wooden homes, crisp mountain breezes, and the clear Baspa River flowing past. Surrounded by rugged peaks and quiet meadows, it captures the cozy, storybook feel of a remote Swiss village. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) Bhandardara: Located in Maharashtra’s Sahyadri hills, Bhandardara brings calm lakes, cascading waterfalls, and mist-draped greenery. Especially inviting during and after monsoon rains, its lush slopes and tranquil waters create a gentle European hillside mood within easy reach of western India. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) Mechuka: Hidden in Arunachal Pradesh, Mechuka blends dramatic mountain backdrops, flowing rivers, and timber cottages in an unhurried setting. Far from mass tourism, its expansive valleys and crisp scenery offer an adventurous yet peaceful escape with distinct highland appeal. (Image: Wikimedia Commons) Kausani: Perched in Uttarakhand’s Bageshwar district, Kausani greets mornings with golden Himalayan sunrises over snow-lined summits. Quiet tea gardens, pine groves, and rich birdlife lend a soothing, postcard-worthy atmosphere ideal for travelers seeking calm mountain views and unhurried days. (Image: Wikimedia Commons)

headline: Dr. Vivek Pathania inaugurates NABARD's Grameen Bharat Mahotsav at the Ridge, Shimla
content: Shimla, 19 November 2026: Dr. Vivek Pathania, Chief General Manager, National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), Himachal Pradesh Regional Office, today inaugurated the Grameen Bharat Mahotsav (GBM) – Himachal Pradesh 2026 at the Padamdev Complex, The Ridge, Shimla. NABARD officials, including Sh. Kushal Deep, DGM, Sh. Pradeep Kumar, DGM, Sh. Himanshu Baliyan and Ms. Vishakha Thapa, attended the inauguration along with others. The Mahotsav runs until 28 November 2026. At 40 stalls, rural artisans, weavers, Self Help Groups (SHGs), Joint Liability Groups (JLGs), Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and Off-Farm Producer Organisations (OFPOs) from 10 states are showing and selling their products. Speaking at the inauguration, Dr. Pathania said, "Grameen Bharat Mahotsav lets our rural producers sell directly to customers. When they meet buyers face to face, they earn better prices, learn what the market wants, learn from the best practices of artisans from other states, and build lasting business links. Every purchase here supports a rural family." Himachal Pradesh is the host state and has 14 stalls from districts across the state. Products on offer include: Producer groups from nine other states are showing GI-tagged and traditional products: The Mahotsav is part of NABARD's work to give rural producers a platform to sell directly to buyers. It brings producers, buyers and institutions together and helps GI-tagged and traditional crafts reach more people. The event supports the national vision of Vocal for Local and Viksit Bharat @2047. headline: Rs 1 land, 99-yr lease: Himachal CM Sukhvinder Sukhu attacks BJP over Baddi allotments
content: Congress legislators on Wednesday staged a protest against the BJP within the premises of the Himachal Pradesh Vidhan Sabha, accusing the previous government of compromising the state’s interests through questionable policy decisions and land allotments. The legislators marched through the Assembly complex ahead of the commencement of House proceedings, raising slogans against the BJP and Leader of Opposition and former Chief Minister Jai Ram Thakur.Addressing mediapersons after the protest, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu launched a sharp attack on the previous BJP regime over the allotment of nearly 5,000 bighas of government land in Baddi to industrialists on a 99-year lease at a token amount of Re 1 under a customised package. He alleged that the allotments were made without registration charges, even as ordinary citizens were required to pay 8 per cent, a rate recently reduced to 4 per cent for women by the present government.Questioning the benefits that Himachal Pradesh had received from these concessions, Sukhu sought details of the industrial investment generated and employment opportunities created for local youth. He announced that his government would introduce a Bill during the ongoing Assembly session to safeguard the state’s resources and facilitate the recovery of land where development work had not begun.Taking a swipe at the BJP’s adjournment motion under Rule 67, the Chief Minister said the provision was intended for serious emergencies and extraordinary circumstances, but the opposition had failed to substantiate its allegations effectively.On allegations of corruption and irregularities in permissions granted under Section 118, Sukhu challenged the BJP to produce documentary evidence, maintaining that his government had not approved permissions involving hundreds of bighas. He assured that appropriate action would follow if credible evidence was presented.The CM also announced an eight-member committee, headed by Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, to prepare a white paper on alleged corruption and irregularities during the previous BJP government’s four-year tenure. Referring to the Himcare health insurance scheme, Sukhu alleged glaring discrepancies in billing records, including claims for hysterectomy procedures involving male patients and testicular surgeries involving women.On Himachal’s financial claims against the BBMB, he asserted that his government was pursuing the state’s rightful interests with political determination, citing the Kishau Dam agreement, Haryana’s affidavit before the Supreme Court and support from the Centre as key aspects of the matter.
